translations.idiomatic: Lin Hong, with appended biographies of Zheng Ding and others; Wang Fu, with Xia Chang appended; Shen Du, with his younger brother Can and appended biographies of Teng Yongheng and others; Nie Danian; Liu Pu, with Su Ping and others appended; Zhang Bi; and Zhang Tai.

translations.idiomatic: Cheng Minzheng; Luo Qi; Chu Guan; Li Mengyang, with appended biographies of Kang Hai, Wang Jiusi, Wang Weizhen, He Jingming, and Xu Zhenqing.

translations.literal: Bian Gong; Gu Lin, younger brother: Lin, with appended biographies: Chen Yi and others; Zheng Shanfu, with appended biographies: Yin Yunxiao, Fang Hao, and others; Lu Shen, with appended biographies: Wang Qi, Wang Tingchen, Li Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Gong; Gu Lin, with his younger brother Lin and appended biographies of Chen Yi and others; Zheng Shanfu, with Yin Yunxiao, Fang Hao, and others appended; Lu Shen, with Wang Qi, Wang Tingchen, and Li Lian appended.

sentences.zh: 林鴻附 鄭定 等

translations.literal: Appended to Lin Hong: Zheng Ding and others.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biographies: Zheng Ding and others.

sentences.zh: 林鴻，字子羽，福清人。

translations.literal: Lin Hong, style name Ziyu, was a native of Fuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Hong, whose style name was Ziyu, came from Fuqing.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，以人才薦，授將樂縣訓導，歷禮部精膳司員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Hongwu reign, he was recommended for his talent, appointed instructor of Jianglo County, and later served as vice director in the Ministry of Rites' Bureau of Refined Provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongwu era he was recommended for his ability, appointed county instructor in Jianglo, and eventually rose to vice director in the Ministry of Rites' Bureau of Refined Provisions.

sentences.zh: 性脫落，不善仕，年未四十自免歸。

translations.literal: By nature he was unconstrained and ill suited to office; before he was forty he resigned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Free-spirited by nature and no good at official life, he resigned and went home before he was forty.

sentences.zh: 閩中善詩者，稱十才子，鴻為之冠。

translations.literal: Those skilled in poetry in Min were called the Ten Talents, and Hong stood at their head.
translations.idiomatic: The finest poets in Fujian were known as the Ten Talents, with Hong foremost among them.

sentences.zh: 十才子者，閩鄭定，侯官王褒、唐泰，長樂高棅、王恭、陳亮，永福王偁及鴻弟子周玄、黃玄，時人目為二玄者也。

translations.literal: The Ten Talents were Zheng Ding of Min, Wang Bao and Tang Tai of Houguan, Gao Bing, Wang Gong, and Chen Liang of Changle, Wang Cheng of Yongfu, and Hong's disciples Zhou Xuan and Huang Xuan, whom contemporaries regarded as the Two Xuans.
translations.idiomatic: The Ten Talents comprised Zheng Ding of Fujian; Wang Bao and Tang Tai of Houguan; Gao Bing, Wang Gong, and Chen Liang of Changle; Wang Cheng of Yongfu; and Hong's pupils Zhou Xuan and Huang Xuan, whom their contemporaries called the Two Xuans.

sentences.zh: 鴻論詩，大指謂漢、魏骨氣雖雄，而菁華不足。

translations.literal: In his discussions of poetry, Hong maintained in general that Han and Wei verse, though vigorous in bone and breath, lacked sufficient refinement.
translations.idiomatic: In his critical writings on poetry, Hong argued broadly that Han and Wei poetry, for all its vigor, lacked sufficient polish.

sentences.zh: 晉祖玄虛，宋尚條暢，齊、梁以下但務春華，少秋實。

translations.literal: Jin took Xuanyan as its ancestor; Song prized lucid flow; from Qi and Liang onward poets pursued only spring blossoms and little autumn fruit.
translations.idiomatic: Jin looked back to the abstruse style; Song favored smooth exposition; from Qi and Liang on, poets cared only for ornamental bloom and seldom for substantial harvest.

sentences.zh: 惟唐作者可謂大成。

translations.literal: Only writers of the Tang may be called fully accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Only Tang poets, in his view, achieved true mastery.

sentences.zh: 然貞觀尚習故陋，神龍漸變常調，開元、天寶間聲律大備，學者當以是為楷式。

translations.literal: Yet the Zhenguan period still clung to old coarseness; the Shenlong era gradually altered the usual mode; between the Kaiyuan and Tianbao reigns tonal rules were fully established, and students ought to take that as their model.
translations.idiomatic: Yet even Zhenguan poetry still bore old roughness; the Shenlong period slowly shifted the conventional style; and between Kaiyuan and Tianbao regulated verse reached its full development—students, he held, should take that as their standard.

sentences.zh: 閩人言詩者率本於鴻。

translations.literal: Those in Min who spoke of poetry generally took Hong as their foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian poets who theorized about verse generally traced their views back to Hong.

sentences.zh: 晉府引禮舍人浦源，字長源，無錫人也。

translations.literal: Pu Yuan of the Jin princely establishment's Directorate of Ceremonial, style name Changyuan, was a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Yuan, a ceremonial attendant in the Jin princely establishment whose style name was Changyuan, came from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 慕鴻名，逾嶺訪之。

translations.literal: Admiring Hong's reputation, he crossed the ranges to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Drawn by Hong's fame, he crossed the mountains into Fujian to seek him out.

sentences.zh: 造其門，二玄請誦所作，曰：「吾家詩也。

translations.literal: When he came to Hong's gate, the Two Xuans asked him to recite what he had written, saying, "This is poetry of our house."
translations.idiomatic: At Hong's door the Two Xuans asked him to recite his work and declared, "This is poetry in our master's line."

sentences.zh: 」鴻延之入社。

translations.literal: " Hong then invited him to join the society.
translations.idiomatic: " Hong then admitted him to their poetry circle.

sentences.zh: 鄭定，字孟宣，嘗為陳友定記室。

translations.literal: Zheng Ding, style name Mengxuan, had once served as secretary to Chen Youding.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Ding, whose style name was Mengxuan, had once been secretary to Chen Youding.

sentences.zh: 友定敗，浮海亡交、廣間。

translations.literal: When Youding was defeated, he fled by sea and wandered between Jiaozhi and Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: After Youding's defeat he put to sea and wandered between Jiaozhi and Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 久之，還居長樂。

translations.literal: After a long while he returned to live in Changle.
translations.idiomatic: After many years he returned to settle in Changle.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，征授延平府訓導，歷國子助教。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign he was summoned and appointed prefectural instructor of Yanping, and later served as assistant instructor at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongwu period he was called to office as prefectural instructor in Yanping and later served as assistant instructor at the National University.

sentences.zh: 王褒，字中美，鴻之兄子婿也。

translations.literal: Wang Bao, style name Zhongmei, was the husband of Hong's elder brother's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao, whose style name was Zhongmei, had married the daughter of Hong's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 為長沙學官，遷永豐知縣。

translations.literal: He served as school official in Changsha and was transferred to be magistrate of Yongfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a school official in Changsha and was later promoted to magistrate of Yongfeng.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，召入，預修《大典》，擢漢府紀善。

translations.literal: During the Yongle reign he was summoned to the capital, took part in compiling the 《Great Compendium》, and was promoted to recorder of the Han princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongle era he was summoned to court, helped compile the 《Yongle Encyclopedia》, and was appointed recorder of the Han princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 唐泰，字亨仲。

translations.literal: Tang Tai, style name Hengzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Tai's style name was Hengzhong.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十七年進士。

translations.literal: He became a presented scholar in the twenty-seventh year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the civil examinations in the twenty-seventh year of Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 歷陝西副使。

translations.literal: He served in succession as vice commissioner in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as vice commissioner in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 高棅，字彥恢，更名廷禮，別號漫士。

translations.literal: Gao Bing, style name Yanhui, later changed his name to Tingli and took the sobriquet Manshi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Bing, whose style name was Yanhui, later adopted the name Tingli and styled himself the Recluse of Idleness.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，以布衣召入翰林，為待詔，遷典籍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy as a commoner, served as a awaiting-edict compiler, and was promoted to archivist.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongle he was summoned to the Hanlin as a commoner, appointed awaiting-edict compiler, and later promoted to archivist.

sentences.zh: 性善飲，工書畫，尤專於詩。

translations.literal: He was fond of drink by nature, skilled in calligraphy and painting, and devoted himself especially to poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine, excelled at calligraphy and painting, and devoted himself above all to poetry.

sentences.zh: 其所選《唐詩品匯》、《唐詩正聲》，終明之世，館閣宗之。

translations.literal: His selections 《Tang Poetry Graded Treasury》 and 《Tang Poetry Correct Sounds》 were revered throughout the Ming by the academies and offices.
translations.idiomatic: His anthologies 《Graded Treasury of Tang Poetry》 and 《Correct Sounds of Tang Poetry》 were revered in court literary circles throughout the Ming.

sentences.zh: 王恭，字安中，隱居七岩山，自稱皆山樵者。

translations.literal: Wang Gong, style name Anzhong, lived in seclusion on Qiyan Mountain and called himself the Woodcutter of Jieshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong, whose style name was Anzhong, lived in seclusion on Qiyan Mountain and styled himself the Woodcutter of Jieshan.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，以儒士薦起待詔翰林，年六十余，與修《大典》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle he was recommended as a Confucian scholar and appointed awaiting-edict compiler in the Hanlin; he was over sixty and took part in compiling the 《Great Compendium》.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongle he was recommended as a scholar and appointed Hanlin awaiting-edict compiler; already past sixty, he helped compile the 《Yongle Encyclopedia》.

sentences.zh: 書成，授翰林院典籍。

translations.literal: When the work was completed he was appointed Hanlin archivist.
translations.idiomatic: When the compilation was finished he was made Hanlin archivist.

sentences.zh: 陳亮，字景明。

translations.literal: Chen Liang, style name Jingming.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Liang's style name was Jingming.

sentences.zh: 自以故元儒生，明興累詔不出，作《陳摶傳》以見志。

translations.literal: Considering himself a former Yuan Confucian scholar, he refused repeated summons after the rise of the Ming and wrote the 《Biography of Chen Tuan》 to express his intent.
translations.idiomatic: As a scholar of the former Yuan, he declined repeated summons after the Ming founding and wrote the 《Biography of Chen Tuan》 to declare his resolve to remain in reclusion.

sentences.zh: 結草屋滄洲中，與三山耆彥為九老會，終其身不仕。

translations.literal: He built a thatched hut on Cangzhou and with venerable worthies of the Three Mountains formed the Society of Nine Elders, never taking office to the end of his life.
translations.idiomatic: He built a thatched hut on the Cangzhou islet, joined the region's elder worthies in a Society of Nine Elders, and never held office for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 王偁，字孟易攵。

translations.literal: Wang Cheng, style name Mengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng, whose style name was Mengyang.

sentences.zh: 父翰仕元，抗節死，偁方九歲，父友吳海撫教之。

translations.literal: His father Han had served the Yuan and died upholding his integrity; Cheng was only nine, and his father's friend Wu Hai reared and taught him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Han had served the Yuan and died refusing submission; Cheng was only nine, and his father's friend Wu Hai brought him up and educated him.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，領鄉薦，入國學，陳情養母。

translations.literal: During Hongwu he received provincial recommendation, entered the National University, and petitioned to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongwu period he received provincial recommendation, entered the National University, and petitioned to return home and care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 母歿，廬墓六年。

translations.literal: When his mother died he dwelt by her tomb in mourning for six years.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he mourned at her grave for six years.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，用薦授翰林檢討，與修《大典》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle, on recommendation he was appointed Hanlin reviser and took part in compiling the 《Great Compendium》.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongle, on recommendation he was appointed Hanlin reviser and helped compile the 《Yongle Encyclopedia》.

sentences.zh: 學博才雄，最為解縉所重。

translations.literal: Learned, broad in knowledge, and powerful in talent, he was most highly regarded by Xie Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Learned and formidably gifted, he won the highest esteem of Xie Jin.

sentences.zh: 自負無輩行，獨推讓同官王洪。

translations.literal: Though confident that he had no peer, he alone yielded precedence to his colleague Wang Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Though he considered himself without equal, he alone deferred to his colleague Wang Hong.

sentences.zh: 王洪者，字希范，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Wang Hong, style name Xifan, was a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong, whose style name was Xifan, came from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 八歲能文，十八成進士，授吏科給事中。

translations.literal: At eight he could write essays; at eighteen he became a presented scholar and was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He could compose essays at eight; at eighteen he passed the examinations and was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 改翰林檢討，偕偁等與修《大典》。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin reviser and together with Cheng and others took part in compiling the 《Great Compendium》.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hanlin reviser and, with Cheng and others, helped compile the 《Yongle Encyclopedia》.

sentences.zh: 歷修撰、侍講。

translations.literal: He served in succession as compiler and lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of compiler and lecturer.

sentences.zh: 帝頒佛曲於塞外，命洪為文，逡巡不應詔。

translations.literal: The emperor distributed Buddhist hymns beyond the frontier and ordered Hong to compose a text, but Hong hesitated and did not respond to the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sent Buddhist hymns to the frontier and ordered Hong to write an accompanying text, Hong hesitated and did not obey.

sentences.zh: 為同列所排，不復進用，卒官。

translations.literal: Ostracized by his colleagues, he was never again promoted and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues turned against him, he was never promoted again, and he died in office.

sentences.zh: 而偁後坐累謫交址，復以縉事連及，系死獄中。

translations.literal: Cheng was later implicated, banished to Jiaozhi, and again entangled in Jin's affair; he was imprisoned and died in jail.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was later implicated in a case, banished to Jiaozhi, and then caught up again in Xie Jin's downfall; he was imprisoned and died in jail.

sentences.zh: 黃玄，字玄之，將樂人。

translations.literal: Huang Xuan, style name Xuanzhi, was a native of Jiangle.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Xuan, whose style name was Xuanzhi, came from Jiangle.

sentences.zh: 聞鴻棄官歸，遂攜妻子居閩縣，以歲貢官泉州訓導。

translations.literal: Hearing that Hong had resigned and returned home, he took wife and children to live in Min County and, through annual tribute student status, became instructor in Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Hong had left office and gone home, he moved his family to Min County and, as a tribute student, became county instructor in Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 周玄，字微之，閩縣人。

translations.literal: Zhou Xuan, style name Weizhi, was a native of Min County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xuan, whose style name was Weizhi, came from Min County.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，以文學征，授禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: During Yongle he was summoned for literary accomplishment and appointed vice director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongle period he was summoned for his literary gifts and appointed vice director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 嘗挾書千卷止高棅家，讀十年，辭去，盡棄其書，曰：「在吾腹笥矣。

translations.literal: He once brought a thousand volumes of books and stayed at Gao Bing's home, reading for ten years; when he left he cast away all the books, saying, "They are in the satchel of my belly."
translations.idiomatic: He once brought a thousand books to Gao Bing's house, read there for ten years, and on leaving discarded them all, saying, "They are stored in the satchel of my belly."

sentences.zh: 」同時趙迪、林敏、陳仲宏、鄭關、林伯璟、張友謙亦以能詩名，皆鴻之弟子。

translations.literal: " At the same time Zhao Di, Lin Min, Chen Zhonghong, Zheng Guan, Lin Bojing, and Zhang Youqian were also famed for poetry; all were Hong's disciples.
translations.idiomatic: " At the same time Zhao Di, Lin Min, Chen Zhonghong, Zheng Guan, Lin Bojing, and Zhang Youqian were also renowned as poets; all were Hong's pupils.

sentences.zh: 王紱附 夏昶

translations.literal: Appended to Wang Fu: Xia Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Xia Chang.

sentences.zh: 王紱，字孟端，無錫人。

translations.literal: Wang Fu, style name Mengduan, was a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu, whose style name was Mengduan, came from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 博學，工歌詩，能書，寫山木竹石，妙絕一時。

translations.literal: Broadly learned, skilled in lyric poetry, able in calligraphy, and in painting mountains, trees, bamboo, and rocks he was unmatched in his age.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned, he excelled at lyric poetry and calligraphy, and his paintings of mountains, trees, bamboo, and rock were unrivaled in his day.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，坐累戍朔州。

translations.literal: During Hongwu he was implicated and garrisoned at Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongwu period he was implicated in a case and sent to garrison duty at Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，用薦，以善書供事文淵閣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle, on recommendation, he served in the Wenyuan Pavilion for his skill in calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongle, on recommendation, he served in the Wenyuan Pavilion on account of his calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 久之，除中書舍人。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed secretarial draftsman in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 紱未仕時，與吳人韓奕為友，隱居九龍山，遂自號九龍山人。

translations.literal: Before Fu took office he was friends with the Wu native Han Yi; they lived in seclusion on Jiulong Mountain, and he styled himself the Man of Jiulong Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Before entering office Fu befriended the Suzhou scholar Han Yi; they lived in seclusion on Jiulong Mountain, and Fu styled himself the Recluse of Jiulong Mountain.

sentences.zh: 於書法，動以古人自期。

translations.literal: In calligraphy he constantly measured himself against the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: In calligraphy he constantly held himself to the standard of the ancients.

sentences.zh: 畫不苟作，遊覽之頃，酒酣握筆，長廊素壁淋漓沾灑。

translations.literal: He did not paint casually; on excursions, when wine was warm in him he would take up the brush and splash long corridors and white walls.
translations.idiomatic: He never painted casually; on outings, once wine had loosened his hand, he would cover long corridors and blank walls in bold, soaking strokes.

sentences.zh: 有投金幣購片楮者，輒拂袖起，或閉門不納，雖豪貴人勿顧也。

translations.literal: If someone offered gold to buy a single sheet, he would brush his sleeve and rise, or shut the door and refuse entry, paying no heed even to the grand and powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who offered gold for a single sheet would find him brush his sleeve and leave, or shut the door; he paid no attention even to the wealthy and powerful.

sentences.zh: 有諫之者，紱曰：「丈夫宜審所處，輕者如此，重者將何以哉！

translations.literal: When someone remonstrated with him, Fu said, "A man ought to weigh where he stands; if he is careless in small things, what will he do in great ones!"
translations.idiomatic: When someone urged him to relent, Fu said, "A man must know his place; if I am careless in small matters, what will I do when great ones arise!"

sentences.zh: 」在京師，月下聞吹簫聲，乘興寫《石竹圖》，明旦訪其人贈之，則估客也。

translations.literal: " In the capital, under the moon he heard the sound of a flute, took inspiration and painted the 《Stone Bamboo》; the next morning he sought out the player to give it to him, and it turned out to be a merchant.
translations.idiomatic: " In the capital he heard a flute under the moon, painted the 《Stone Bamboo》 on impulse, and the next morning sought out the player to give him the picture—it was a merchant.

sentences.zh: 客以紅氍毹饋，請再寫一枝為配。

translations.literal: The guest presented a red felt rug and asked him to paint another spray as a pair.
translations.idiomatic: The merchant offered a red felt rug and asked him to paint a matching spray.

sentences.zh: 紱索前畫裂之，還其饋。

translations.literal: Fu demanded the earlier painting back, tore it apart, and returned the gift.
translations.idiomatic: Fu demanded the earlier painting back, tore it up, and returned the gift.

sentences.zh: 一日退朝，黔國公沐晟從後呼其字，紱不應。

translations.literal: One day after leaving court, the Prince of Qian Mu Cheng called his style name from behind, and Fu did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: One day after court, Prince Mu Cheng of Qian called his style name from behind, and Fu did not respond.

sentences.zh: 同列語之曰：「此黔國公也。

translations.literal: A colleague told him, "That is the Prince of Qian."
translations.idiomatic: A colleague told him, "That was the Prince of Qian."

sentences.zh: 」紱曰：「我非不聞之，是必與我索畫耳。

translations.literal: " Fu said, "It is not that I did not hear; he must certainly be coming to ask me for a painting."
translations.idiomatic: " Fu said, "I heard him well enough—he surely means to ask me for a painting."

sentences.zh: 」晟走及之，果以畫請，紱頷之而已。

translations.literal: " Cheng ran up to him and indeed asked for a painting; Fu only nodded.
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng caught up with him and, as expected, asked for a painting; Fu merely nodded.

sentences.zh: 逾數年，晟復以書來，紱始為作畫。

translations.literal: After several years Cheng wrote again, and only then did Fu paint for him.
translations.idiomatic: Years later Cheng wrote again, and only then did Fu paint for him.

sentences.zh: 既而曰：「我畫直遺黔公不可。

translations.literal: Then he said, "I cannot simply give this painting straight to the Prince of Qian."
translations.idiomatic: Then he said, "I cannot simply give this painting directly to the Prince of Qian."

sentences.zh: 黔公客平仲微者，我友也，以友故與之，俟黔公與求則可耳。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qian's guest Ping Zhongwei is my friend; for friendship's sake I give it to him, and when the prince himself asks for it, that will do.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's guest Ping Zhongwei is my friend; I give it to him as a friend, and when the prince himself asks for it, that will be enough.

sentences.zh: 」其高介絕俗如此。

translations.literal: " Such was his lofty integrity and distance from the vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was his lofty, uncompromising character.

sentences.zh: 昆山夏昶者，亦善畫竹石，亞於紱。

translations.literal: Xia Chang of Kunshan was also skilled at painting bamboo and rock, second only to Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Chang of Kunshan also excelled at bamboo and rock painting, though a step below Fu.

sentences.zh: 畫竹一枝，直白金一錠，然人多以饋遺得之。

translations.literal: A single spray of bamboo was worth a full ingot of white gold, yet most people obtained his work through gifts.
translations.idiomatic: A single spray of bamboo fetched a full ingot of silver, yet most people obtained his work as gifts rather than payment.

sentences.zh: 昶，字仲昭，永樂十三年進士，改庶吉士，歷官太常寺卿。

translations.literal: Chang, style name Zhongzhao, became a presented scholar in the thirteenth year of Yongle, was made a Hanlin bachelor, and served in succession as director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, whose style name was Zhongzhao, passed the examinations in the thirteenth year of Yongle, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and eventually became director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 昶與上元張益，同中進士，同以文名，同善畫竹。

translations.literal: Chang and Zhang Yi of Shangyuan passed the examinations in the same year, were famed alike for literature, and were alike skilled at painting bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Chang and Zhang Yi of Shangyuan passed the examinations together, shared a literary reputation, and both excelled at bamboo painting.

sentences.zh: 其後，昶見益《石渠閣賦》，自謂不如，遂不復作賦。

translations.literal: Later, when Chang saw Yi's rhapsody 《Stone Channel Pavilion》, he declared himself inferior and never wrote rhapsodies again.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Chang read Yi's rhapsody 《Stone Channel Pavilion》, he judged himself inferior and never wrote rhapsodies again.

sentences.zh: 益見昶所畫竹石，亦遂不復畫竹。

translations.literal: When Yi saw the bamboo and rock that Chang had painted, he too never painted bamboo again.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi saw Chang's bamboo and rock paintings, he too gave up painting bamboo.

sentences.zh: 益死土木之難。

translations.literal: Yi died in the Tumu disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Yi died in the Tumu crisis.

sentences.zh: 仲微，名顯，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Zhongwei, personal name Xian, was a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwei, whose personal name was Xian, came from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 嘗知滕縣事，謫戍雲南。

translations.literal: He had once served as magistrate of Teng County and was banished to garrison duty in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He had served as magistrate of Teng County and was later banished to garrison duty in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 其為詩頗豪放自喜，雲南詩人稱平、居、陳、郭，顯其一也。

translations.literal: His poetry was quite bold and free, and he took pride in it; Yunnan poets spoke of Ping, Ju, Chen, and Guo, and Xian was one of them.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry was boldly self-assured; Yunnan poets spoke of the quartet Ping, Ju, Chen, and Guo, and Xian was one of them.

sentences.zh: 沈度弟 粲 附 滕用亨 等

translations.literal: Shen Du, younger brother Can, with appended biographies: Teng Yongheng and others.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Du, with his younger brother Can and appended biographies of Teng Yongheng and others.

sentences.zh: 昆山夏昺者，字孟晹，與其弟昶以善書畫聞，同官中書舍人，時號大小中書，而度、粲號大小學士。

translations.literal: Xia Bing of Kunshan, style name Mengyang, and his younger brother Chang were famed for skill in calligraphy and painting; both served as secretaries in the Secretariat and were called the Greater and Lesser Secretaries, while Du and Can were called the Greater and Lesser Academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Bing of Kunshan, whose style name was Mengyang, and his younger brother Chang were renowned for calligraphy and painting; both served as secretarial draftsmen and were nicknamed the Greater and Lesser Secretaries, while Du and Can were nicknamed the Greater and Lesser Academicians.

sentences.zh: 度性敦實，謙以下人，嚴取與。

translations.literal: Du was sincere and solid by nature, humble toward those below him, and strict in what he accepted and gave.
translations.idiomatic: Du was sincere and steady by nature, humble toward others, and strict about what he accepted or gave.

sentences.zh: 有訓導介其友求書，請識姓字於上。

translations.literal: A county instructor introduced his friend to ask for calligraphy and requested that his surname and personal name be inscribed on it.
translations.idiomatic: A county instructor introduced a friend who asked for a piece of calligraphy and requested that his name be inscribed on it.

sentences.zh: 度沈思曰：「得非曩訐奏有司者耶？

translations.literal: Du pondered and said, "Might this not be the one who formerly lodged accusations against me with the authorities?"
translations.idiomatic: Du thought a moment and said, "Is this not the man who once denounced me to the authorities?"

sentences.zh: 」遽卻之。

translations.literal: " He immediately refused.
translations.idiomatic: " He refused at once.

sentences.zh: 其友固請，終不肯書姓名。

translations.literal: His friend repeatedly pressed him, but in the end he would not write his name.
translations.idiomatic: His friend pressed him again and again, yet he still refused to inscribe his name.

sentences.zh: 其在內廷備顧問，必以正對。

translations.literal: When he served in the inner court as advisor, he always answered with direct rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: As a consultant in the inner court, he always answered forthrightly and without evasion.

sentences.zh: 粲篤於事兄，己有賜，輒歸其兄。

translations.literal: Can was deeply devoted in serving his elder brother; whenever he himself received gifts, he immediately gave them to his brother.
translations.idiomatic: Can was devoted to his elder brother; whatever gifts he received, he at once turned over to him.

sentences.zh: 滕用亨，初名權，字用衡。

translations.literal: Teng Yongheng, whose original name was Quan and whose style name was Yongheng.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Yongheng was originally named Quan and styled Yongheng.

sentences.zh: 精篆隸書。

translations.literal: He excelled at seal and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: He was a master of seal and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 被薦時年七十矣，召見，大書麟鳳龜龍四字以進，又獻《貞符詩》三篇。

translations.literal: When recommended, he was already seventy years old; summoned for an audience, he wrote large characters—unicorn, phoenix, tortoise, and dragon—to present, and also offered three pieces from the 《Odes of Auspicious Signs》.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he was recommended he was seventy. Called to audience, he wrote the four characters unicorn, phoenix, tortoise, and dragon in large script as his tribute, and also presented three poems from his 《Odes of Auspicious Signs》.

sentences.zh: 授翰林待詔，與修《永樂大典》。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin awaiting-edict compiler and took part in compiling the 《Yongle Encyclopedia》.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin awaiting-edict compiler and helped compile the 《Yongle Encyclopedia》.

sentences.zh: 用亨善鑒古，嘗侍帝觀畫卷，未竟，眾目為趙伯駒，用亨曰：「此王詵筆也。

translations.literal: Yongheng was skilled at appraising antiquities; once, while attending the emperor in viewing a scroll of painting that was not yet finished, everyone took it for the work of Zhao Boju, but Yongheng said, "This is the brushwork of Wang Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Yongheng had a keen eye for antiquities. Once, while attending the emperor as he viewed a painting scroll still unrolled to its end, all eyes took it for Zhao Boju's work. Yongheng said, "This is Wang Shen's brush.

sentences.zh: 」至卷尾，果然。

translations.literal: " Reaching the end of the scroll, it proved to be so.
translations.idiomatic: " At the end of the scroll, he was proved right.

sentences.zh: 陳登，字思孝。

translations.literal: Chen Deng, whose style name was Sixiao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Deng, styled Sixiao.

sentences.zh: 初仕羅田縣丞，改蘭溪，再改浮梁。

translations.literal: He first served as assistant magistrate of Luotian County, was transferred to Lanxi, and then transferred again to Fuliang.
translations.idiomatic: He began as assistant magistrate of Luotian, then served in Lanxi and afterward in Fuliang.

sentences.zh: 選入翰林，仍給縣丞祿，歷十年始授中書舍人。

translations.literal: Selected into the Hanlin, he still received the salary of an assistant magistrate; only after ten years was he appointed Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Chosen for the Hanlin, he continued to draw an assistant magistrate's salary for ten years before he was finally made a Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 登於六書本原，博考詳究，用力甚勤。

translations.literal: Deng, regarding the original sources of the Six Scripts, broadly investigated and examined them in detail, exerting himself with great diligence.
translations.idiomatic: In the origins of the Six Scripts, Deng read widely, examined closely, and labored with exceptional diligence.

sentences.zh: 自周、秦以來，殘碑斷碣，必窮搜摩搨審度而辨定之。

translations.literal: From the Zhou and Qin onward, whenever he encountered broken steles and truncated tablets, he would exhaustively search them out, rub and copy them, scrutinize them, and determine their readings.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhou and Qin times onward, he tracked down every broken stele and truncated tablet he could find, made rubbings, weighed the evidence, and settled their readings.

sentences.zh: 得其傳者，太常卿南城程南雲也。

translations.literal: The one who received his transmission was Cheng Nanyun of Nancheng, minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His tradition passed to Cheng Nanyun of Nancheng, minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 聶大年

translations.literal: Nie Danian
translations.idiomatic: Nie Danian

sentences.zh: 聶大年，字壽卿，臨川人。

translations.literal: Nie Danian, whose style name was Shouqing, was a man of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Danian, styled Shouqing, came from Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 父同文，洪武中，官翰林侍書、中書舍人。

translations.literal: His father Tongwen, during the Hongwu era, served as Hanlin attendant scribe and Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tongwen served in the Hongwu era as Hanlin attendant scribe and Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 燕王入京師，迎謁，道曷死，死後五月而大年生，母胡撫之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan entered the capital, Tongwen went out to greet and pay homage, but died on the road; five months after his death Danian was born, and his mother Hu raised him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan entered the capital, Tongwen went out to greet him but died on the road. Danian was born five months later, and his mother Hu brought him up.

sentences.zh: 比長，博學，善詩古文。

translations.literal: When he had grown up, he was broadly learned and skilled in classical poetry and prose.
translations.idiomatic: Once grown, he was widely read and gifted in classical poetry and prose.

sentences.zh: 葉盛稱其詩，謂三十年來絕唱也。

translations.literal: Ye Sheng praised his poetry, saying that for thirty years there had been nothing to match it.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Sheng hailed his poetry as unmatched for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 書得歐陽率更法。

translations.literal: In calligraphy he mastered the method of Ouyang the Commandant of Rate-Setting.
translations.idiomatic: In calligraphy he mastered the style of Ouyang Xun.

sentences.zh: 宣德末，薦授仁和訓導。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xuande era, on recommendation he was appointed county instructor of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xuande, on recommendation he was appointed county instructor of Renhe.

sentences.zh: 母卒，歸葬，哀感行路。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he returned home to bury her, and his grief moved passersby on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he went home to bury her, and his mourning moved all who passed by.

sentences.zh: 裡人列其母子賢行上之有司，詔旌其門。

translations.literal: Villagers set forth the worthy conduct of mother and son and submitted it to the authorities, and an edict was issued to honor their household.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors reported the mother and son's virtuous conduct to the authorities, and the court issued an edict honoring their household.

sentences.zh: 服闋，分教常州，遷仁和教諭。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete, he was assigned to teach at Changzhou and was later transferred to county instructor of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning, he was posted to teach at Changzhou and later promoted to county instructor of Renhe.

sentences.zh: 景泰六年薦入翰林，未幾得疾卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jingtai he was recommended into the Hanlin; before long he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jingtai he was recommended into the Hanlin, but soon afterward fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 始，尚書王直以詩寄錢塘戴文進索畫，自序昔與文進交，嘗戲作詩一聯，至是十年始成之。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Minister Wang Zhi sent a poem to Dai Wenjin of Qiantang asking for a painting; in his preface he said that he and Wenjin had been friends of old and had once playfully composed one couplet of poetry, and only now, ten years later, had he completed it.
translations.idiomatic: Once, Minister Wang Zhi sent a poem to Dai Wenjin of Qiantang requesting a painting. In a preface he explained that he and Wenjin had long been friends, that they had once playfully drafted a couplet, and that only now, ten years later, had he finished the poem.

sentences.zh: 大年題其後曰：「公愛文進之畫，十年不忘。

translations.literal: Danian inscribed afterward and said, "Your Excellency loves Wenjin's painting and has not forgotten it for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Danian added an inscription at the end: "Your Excellency loves Wenjin's painting and has not forgotten it in ten years.

sentences.zh: 使以是心待天下賢者，天下寧復有遣賢哉。

translations.literal: If you treated all worthy men under Heaven with such a heart, would there still be worthy men cast aside under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: If you treated every worthy man in the realm with such constancy, would any talent still be left neglected?

sentences.zh: 」直聞其言，不怒亦不薦。

translations.literal: " When Zhi heard these words, he was neither angry nor recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhi heard this, but neither took offense nor recommended him.

sentences.zh: 及大年疾篤，作詩貽直，有「鏡中白髮孰憐我，湖上青山欲待誰」句，直曰，「此欲吾志其墓耳」，遂為之志。

translations.literal: When Danian's illness grew grave, he composed a poem and sent it to Zhi, containing the lines, "Who in the mirror pities my white hair? On the lake, the green hills seem to wait for whom?" Zhi said, "This is asking me to compose his tomb inscription," and so he wrote one for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Danian's illness turned grave, he sent Zhi a poem with the lines, "Who in the mirror pities my white hair? On the lake, the green hills seem to wait for whom?" Zhi said, "He wants me to write his epitaph," and did so.

sentences.zh: 劉溥附 蘇平 等

translations.literal: Liu Pu, with appended biographies: Su Ping and others.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pu, with Su Ping and others appended.

sentences.zh: 劉溥，字原博，長洲人。

translations.literal: Liu Pu, whose style name was Yuanbo, was a man of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pu, styled Yuanbo, came from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖彥，父士賓，皆以醫得官。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan and his father Shibin both obtained office through medicine.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan and his father Shibin both won office through medicine.

sentences.zh: 溥八歲賦《溝水詩》，時目為聖童。

translations.literal: At eight years old Pu composed the 《Ditch Water Poem》, and at the time he was regarded as a divine child.
translations.idiomatic: At eight Pu wrote the 《Ditch Water Poem》, and people already hailed him as a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 長侍祖父游兩京，研究經史兼通天文、曆數。

translations.literal: Growing up, he attended his grandfather and traveled the two capitals, studying the classics and histories and also mastering astronomy and calendrical calculation.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he accompanied his grandfather between the two capitals, studying the classics and histories while also mastering astronomy and calendrical science.

sentences.zh: 宣德時，以文學征。

translations.literal: During the Xuande era he was summoned for his literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuande era he was summoned for his literary attainments.

sentences.zh: 有言溥善醫者，授惠民局副使，調太醫院吏目。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Pu was skilled in medicine, so he was appointed vice commissioner of the Bureau of Public Welfare Medicine and was transferred to clerk of the Imperial Medical Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court that Pu was also skilled in medicine, he was made vice commissioner of the Bureau of Public Welfare Medicine and later transferred to clerk of the Imperial Medical Academy.

sentences.zh: 恥以醫自名，日吟詠為事。

translations.literal: Ashamed to make a name for himself through medicine, he made daily poetry his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed to be known as a physician, he devoted himself to poetry.

sentences.zh: 其詩初學西昆，後更奇縱，與湯胤勣、蘇平、蘇正、沈愚、王淮、晏鐸、鄒亮、蔣忠、王貞慶號「景泰十才子」，溥為主盟。

translations.literal: His poetry at first studied the Western Kun style, then became even more strange and unrestrained; together with Tang Yinji, Su Ping, Su Zheng, Shen Yu, Wang Huai, Yan Duo, Zou Liang, Jiang Zhong, and Wang Zhenqing he was styled the "Ten Talents of the Jingtai Era," with Pu as their leader.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry began in the Western Kun manner and later turned bolder and more unrestrained. With Tang Yinji, Su Ping, Su Zheng, Shen Yu, Wang Huai, Yan Duo, Zou Liang, Jiang Zhong, and Wang Zhenqing he was known as one of the "Ten Talents of the Jingtai Era," and Pu was their acknowledged leader.

sentences.zh: 胤勣，東甌王和曾孫，自有傳。

translations.literal: Yinji was the great-grandson of the Prince of Dong'ou, He; he has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yinji was the great-grandson of Prince He of Dong'ou and has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 蘇平，字秉衡，弟正，字秉貞，海寧人。

translations.literal: Su Ping, whose style name was Bingheng, and his younger brother Zheng, whose style name was Bingzhen, were men of Haining.
translations.idiomatic: Su Ping, styled Bingheng, and his younger brother Zheng, styled Bingzhen, came from Haining.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並以布衣終。

translations.literal: Both brothers ended their lives as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers lived out their lives as commoners.

sentences.zh: 沈愚，字通理，昆山人，業醫終其身。

translations.literal: Shen Yu, whose style name was Tongli, was a man of Kunshan and practiced medicine all his life.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yu, styled Tongli, came from Kunshan and practiced medicine to the end of his days.

sentences.zh: 王淮，字柏源，慈溪人。

translations.literal: Wang Huai, whose style name was Baiyuan, was a man of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huai, styled Baiyuan, came from Cixi.

sentences.zh: 晏鐸，字振之，富順人。

translations.literal: Yan Duo, whose style name was Zhenzhi, was a man of Fushun.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Duo, styled Zhenzhi, came from Fushun.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士授御史，歷按兩畿、山東，所至有聲。

translations.literal: From probationary Hanlin compiler he was appointed censor and successively inspected the two capital regions and Shandong; wherever he went he won renown.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as a probationary Hanlin compiler, he was appointed censor and toured the two capital regions and Shandong as inspecting commissioner, winning a reputation wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 坐言事謫上高典史，鄰境寇發，官兵不能討，鐸捕滅之，歸所掠於民。

translations.literal: Because of a memorial on public affairs he was demoted to county clerk of Shanggao; when bandits rose in a neighboring district and government troops could not suppress them, Duo captured and destroyed them and returned what had been plundered to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted to county clerk of Shanggao for a memorial on public affairs, he later crushed bandits in a neighboring district when regular troops could not, and restored the loot to the people.

sentences.zh: 鄒亮，字克明，長洲人。

translations.literal: Zou Liang, whose style name was Keming, was a man of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Liang, styled Keming, came from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 用況鐘薦，擢吏部司務，遷御史。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Kuang Zhong he was promoted to clerk in the Ministry of Personnel and was later transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Kuang Zhong, he was promoted to clerk in the Ministry of Personnel and later made censor.

sentences.zh: 蔣忠，字主忠，儀真人，徙居句容。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhong, whose style name was Zhuzhong, was a man of Yizhen and later moved to Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhong, styled Zhuzhong, was from Yizhen and later moved to Jurong.

sentences.zh: 王貞慶，字善甫，駙馬都尉寧子也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhenqing, whose style name was Shanfu, was the son of the Prince Consort of Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhenqing, styled Shanfu, was the son of the Prince Consort of Ning.

sentences.zh: 折節好士，有詩名，時稱金粟公子。

translations.literal: He lowered himself to befriend men of talent, had a reputation in poetry, and at the time was called the Young Master of Golden Millet.
translations.idiomatic: He humbled himself to befriend scholars, won renown as a poet, and was known in his day as the Young Master of Golden Millet.

sentences.zh: 張弼，字汝弼，松江華亭人。

translations.literal: Zhang Bi, whose style name was Rubi, was a man of Huating in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bi, styled Rubi, came from Huating in Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 成化二年進士。

translations.literal: He became a presented scholar in the second year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the palace examination in the second year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 授兵部主事，進員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed secretary in the Ministry of War and was promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed secretary in the Ministry of War and later promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 遷南安知府，地當兩廣沖，奸人聚山谷為惡，悉捕滅之。

translations.literal: Transferred to prefect of Nan'an, a place at the strategic crossing of the two Guang regions, he captured and destroyed wicked men who had gathered in the mountain valleys to do evil.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Nan'an, a frontier post between the two Guang regions, he rooted out bandits who had gathered in the hills and ravines.

sentences.zh: 毀淫祠百數十區，建為社學。

translations.literal: He destroyed more than a hundred illicit shrines and built community schools in their place.
translations.idiomatic: He tore down more than a hundred illicit shrines and converted the sites into community schools.

sentences.zh: 謝病歸，士民為立祠。

translations.literal: He resigned on grounds of illness and returned home, and officials and commoners erected a shrine to him.
translations.idiomatic: He retired citing illness, and local officials and people erected a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 弼自幼穎拔，善詩文，工草書，怪偉跌宕，震撼一世。

translations.literal: Bi from youth was sharp and outstanding, skilled in poetry and prose, and adept at cursive script—strange, grand, and unrestrained, shaking his age.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was precocious, gifted in poetry and prose, and a master of cursive script—bold, strange, and sweeping enough to startle his generation.

sentences.zh: 自號東海。

translations.literal: He styled himself Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: He took the sobriquet Donghai, the Eastern Sea.

sentences.zh: 張東海之名，流播外裔。

translations.literal: The name Zhang Donghai spread even to foreign lands.
translations.idiomatic: The name Zhang Donghai spread even beyond the borders.

sentences.zh: 為詩，信手縱筆，多不屬稿，即有所屬，以書故，輒為人持去。

translations.literal: When composing poetry he wrote freely at will; mostly he did not draft beforehand, and even when he did, because of his calligraphy people would carry the drafts away.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote poetry freely, seldom bothering with drafts; when he did, admirers of his calligraphy usually carried the pages off.

sentences.zh: 與李東陽、謝鐸善。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Li Dongyang and Xie Duo.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Li Dongyang and Xie Duo.

sentences.zh: 嘗自言：「吾平生，書不如詩，詩不如文。

translations.literal: He once said of himself, "In my life, calligraphy is inferior to poetry, and poetry is inferior to prose.
translations.idiomatic: He once said of himself, "In my life, my calligraphy falls short of my poetry, and my poetry falls short of my prose.

sentences.zh: 」東陽戲之曰：「英雄欺人每如此，不足信也。

translations.literal: " Dongyang jokingly said to him, "Heroes deceive people just like this—it cannot be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: " Dongyang teased him, "Heroes always talk like this—it is not to be believed.

sentences.zh: 」鐸稱其好學不倦，詩文成一家言。

translations.literal: " Xie Duo praised his untiring love of learning and said his poetry and prose formed a distinctive school of his own.
translations.idiomatic: " Xie Duo praised his tireless love of learning and said his poetry and prose formed a school of his own.

sentences.zh: 子弘至，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Hongzhi has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongzhi has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 張泰

translations.literal: Zhang Tai
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tai

sentences.zh: （陸釴 陸容）〉

translations.literal: (Lu Yin, Lu Rong)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Lu Yin and Lu Rong)〉

sentences.zh: 張泰，字亨父，太倉人。

translations.literal: Zhang Tai, whose style name was Hengfu, was a man of Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tai, styled Hengfu, came from Taicang.

sentences.zh: 陸釴，字鼎儀，昆山人。

translations.literal: Lu Yin, whose style name was Dingyi, was a man of Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yin, styled Dingyi, came from Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 陸容，字文量，亦太倉人。

translations.literal: Lu Rong, whose style name was Wenliang, was also a man of Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Rong, styled Wenliang, was also from Taicang.

sentences.zh: 三人少齊名，號「婁東三鳳」。

translations.literal: The three from youth shared equal fame and were styled the "Three Phoenixes of Loudong."
translations.idiomatic: The three were equally famous from youth and were known as the "Three Phoenixes of Loudong."

sentences.zh: 泰舉天順八年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討，遷修撰。

translations.literal: Tai passed the palace examination in the eighth year of Tianshun, was selected as probationary Hanlin compiler, was appointed reviser, and was transferred to compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Tai passed the palace examination in the eighth year of Tianshun, entered the Hanlin as a probationer, and rose from reviser to compiler.

sentences.zh: 為人恬淡自守，詩名亞李東陽。

translations.literal: By nature he was tranquil and self-restrained, and in poetic reputation he ranked next to Li Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet and self-contained by nature, he stood second only to Li Dongyang in poetic reputation.

sentences.zh: 弘治間，藝苑皆稱李懷麓、張滄洲，東陽有《懷麓堂集》，泰有《滄洲集》也。

translations.literal: During the Hongzhi era, literary circles all spoke of Li Huailu and Zhang Cangzhou; Dongyang had the 《Collection from the Hall of Reverence for the Foothills》, and Tai had the 《Collection from Cangzhou》.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongzhi era literary circles spoke of Li Huailu and Zhang Cangzhou—Dongyang with his 《Collection from the Hall of Reverence for the Foothills》 and Tai with his 《Collection from Cangzhou》.

sentences.zh: 釴與泰同年進士，殿試第二。

translations.literal: Yin and Tai became presented scholars in the same year, and Yin placed second in the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and Tai passed the palace examination in the same year, with Yin ranking second.

sentences.zh: 授編修，歷修撰、諭德。

translations.literal: He was appointed compiler, and successively served as compiler and preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed compiler and later served as compiler and preceptor.

sentences.zh: 孝宗立，以東宮講讀勞，進太常少卿兼侍讀，得疾歸。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne, in recognition of his labors lecturing in the Eastern Palace he was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and concurrent palace reader, then fell ill and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong came to the throne, he was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and concurrent palace reader for his service lecturing in the Eastern Palace, but soon fell ill and retired.

sentences.zh: 泰、釴皆早卒。

translations.literal: Both Tai and Yin died early.
translations.idiomatic: Both Tai and Yin died young.

sentences.zh: 容，成化中進士。

translations.literal: Rong became a presented scholar during the Chenghua era.
translations.idiomatic: Rong passed the palace examination in the Chenghua era.

sentences.zh: 授南京主事，進兵部職方郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed secretary in Nanjing and was promoted to director in the Ministry of War's Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed secretary in Nanjing and later promoted to director in the Ministry of War's Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 西番進獅子，奏請大臣往迎，容諫止之。

translations.literal: When the Western tribes presented a lion, a memorial requested that a high minister go to receive it, but Rong remonstrated and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: When Western tribes presented a lion, the court proposed sending a high minister to receive it, but Rong remonstrated and had the plan stopped.

sentences.zh: 遷浙江參政，罷歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner of Zhejiang and was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice commissioner of Zhejiang, then dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 程敏政

translations.literal: Cheng Minzheng
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Minzheng

sentences.zh: 程敏政，字克勤，休寧人，南京兵部尚書信子也。

translations.literal: Cheng Minzheng, whose style name was Keqin, was a man of Xiuning and the son of Xin, minister of war at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Minzheng, styled Keqin, came from Xiuning and was the son of Xin, minister of war at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 十歲侍父官四川，巡撫羅綺以神童薦。

translations.literal: At ten years old he attended his father in office in Sichuan, and Grand Coordinator Luo Qi recommended him as a divine child.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he accompanied his father to his post in Sichuan, and Grand Coordinator Luo Qi recommended him as a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 英宗召試，悅之，詔讀書翰林院，給廩饌。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong summoned him for examination, was pleased with him, and ordered that he study in the Hanlin Academy and be granted stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong tested him, was delighted, and ordered him to study in the Hanlin Academy with a stipend.

sentences.zh: 學士李賢、彭時咸愛重之，賢以女妻焉。

translations.literal: Academicians Li Xian and Peng Shi all loved and valued him, and Xian gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Academicians Li Xian and Peng Shi both cherished him, and Xian gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 成化二年進士及第，授編修，歷左諭德，直講東宮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua he passed the palace examination with highest honors, was appointed compiler, successively served as left preceptor, and lectured directly in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He placed first in the palace examination in the second year of Chenghua, was appointed compiler, rose to left preceptor, and lectured in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 翰林中，學問該博稱敏政，文章古雅稱李東陽，性行真純稱陳音，各為一時冠。

translations.literal: Within the Hanlin, for comprehensive learning Minzheng was praised, for classical prose Li Dongyang was praised, and for character and conduct Chen Yin was praised; each was foremost of his time.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hanlin, Minzheng was hailed for breadth of learning, Li Dongyang for classical prose, and Chen Yin for purity of character—each the leading figure of his day.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嗣位，以宮僚恩擢少詹事兼侍講學士，直經筵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong succeeded to the throne, in recognition of his service as a palace official he was promoted to junior grand secretary and concurrent expositor-in-waiting, and lectured directly at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong succeeded, he was promoted to junior grand secretary and concurrent expositor-in-waiting for his service in the Eastern Palace, and lectured at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 敏政名臣子，才高負文學，常俯視儕偶，頗為人所疾。

translations.literal: Minzheng was the son of a famous minister, talented and proud of his literary learning, and often looked down on his peers, which greatly aroused resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: As the son of a distinguished minister, Minzheng was gifted and proud of his literary attainments, often looked down on his peers, and drew considerable resentment.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年冬，御史王嵩等以雨災劾敏政，因勒致仕。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Hongzhi, Censor Wang Song and others impeached Minzheng on account of rain disasters, and he was compelled to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Hongzhi, Censor Wang Song and others impeached Minzheng over rain disasters, and he was forced to retire.

sentences.zh: 五年起官，尋改太常卿兼侍讀學士，掌院事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was recalled to office, and soon was changed to minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and concurrent reader-in-waiting, directing the affairs of the academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was recalled, and soon made minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and concurrent reader-in-waiting, with charge of the academy.

sentences.zh: 進禮部右侍郎，專典內閣誥敕。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of the right in the Ministry of Rites and was charged exclusively with drafting edicts and commissions for the inner cabinet.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of rites on the right and put in charge of drafting edicts and commissions for the inner cabinet.

sentences.zh: 十二年與李東陽主會試，舉人徐經、唐寅預作文，與試題合。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he and Li Dongyang presided over the metropolitan examination; the presented scholars Xu Jing and Tang Yin had prepared compositions in advance that matched the examination topics.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he and Li Dongyang presided over the metropolitan examination, and the candidates Xu Jing and Tang Yin were found to have prepared essays in advance that matched the examination topics.

sentences.zh: 給事中華昶劾敏政鬻題，時榜未發，詔敏政毋閱卷，其所錄者令東陽會同考官覆校。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Hua Chang impeached Minzheng for selling examination topics. The roster had not yet been published. An edict ordered Minzheng not to grade papers, and those he had passed were to be jointly re-examined by Dongyang and the examiners.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Hua Chang impeached Cheng Minzheng for selling examination topics. The results list had not yet been released, and an edict barred Minzheng from grading papers and ordered Li Dongyang and the examiners to re-check every candidate he had passed.

sentences.zh: 二人卷皆不在所取中，東陽以聞，言者猶不已。

translations.literal: Neither man's paper was among those selected. Dongyang reported this, yet the critics still would not let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: Neither man's paper was among those selected. Li Dongyang reported this to the throne, but the accusers still would not let the matter rest.

sentences.zh: 敏政、昶、經、寅俱下獄，坐經嘗贄見敏政，寅嘗從敏政乞文，黜為吏，敏政勒致仕，而昶以言事不實調南太僕主簿。

translations.literal: Minzheng, Chang, Jing, and Yin were all imprisoned. Jing was condemned because he had once presented a gift when calling on Minzheng, and Yin because he had once asked Minzheng for compositions; they were demoted to clerks. Minzheng was compelled to retire, while Chang, for making accusations not borne out by fact, was transferred to be chief secretary of the Southern Court of Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Minzheng, Chang, Jing, and Yin were all imprisoned. Jing was punished because he had once presented a gift when calling on Minzheng, and Yin because he had once asked Minzheng for compositions; both were demoted to clerks. Minzheng was forced to retire, while Chang, for lodging accusations not borne out by the facts, was transferred to chief secretary of the Southern Court of Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 敏政出獄憤恚，發癰卒。

translations.literal: After leaving prison Minzheng was consumed by anger and resentment; an abscess broke out and he died.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving prison Minzheng was consumed by anger and resentment; an abscess broke out and he died.

sentences.zh: 後贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously granted the title of minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously granted the title of minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 或言敏政之獄，傅瀚欲奪其位，令昶奏之。

translations.literal: Some said that in Minzheng's case Fu Han had wanted to seize his position and had Chang bring the accusation.
translations.idiomatic: Some said that in Minzheng's case Fu Han had wanted to seize his post and had Hua Chang lodge the accusation.

sentences.zh: 事秘，莫能明也。

translations.literal: The affair was secret, and no one could clarify it.
translations.idiomatic: The affair was kept secret, and no one could establish the truth.

sentences.zh: 羅，字景鳴，南城人。

translations.literal: Luo Qi, styled Jingming, was a man of Nancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Qi, styled Jingming, came from Nancheng.

sentences.zh: 博學，好古文，務為奇奧。

translations.literal: Broadly learned, he loved ancient prose and strove to make his writing strange and abstruse.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned, he loved ancient prose and strove to make his writing strange and abstruse.

sentences.zh: 年四十困諸生，輸粟入國學。

translations.literal: At forty he was still stuck as a licentiate and submitted grain to enter the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At forty he was still only a licentiate and paid grain to gain entry to the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 丘浚為祭酒，議南人不得留北監。

translations.literal: Qiu Jun was chancellor and proposed that southerners should not be permitted to remain at the northern directorate.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiu Jun was chancellor, he proposed that southerners should not be allowed to remain at the northern Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 固請不已，浚罵之曰：「若識幾字，倔強乃爾！

translations.literal: Qi kept pressing his plea without stop. Jun berated him, saying, "You know only a few characters—how can you be so stubborn!
translations.idiomatic: Qi kept pressing his plea without letup. Qiu Jun berated him, saying, "You know only a handful of characters—how can you be so stubborn!

sentences.zh: 」仰對曰：「惟中秘書未讀耳。

translations.literal: " Qi looked up and replied, "It is only the Central Secretariat books I have not yet read."
translations.idiomatic: " Qi looked up and replied, "It is only the books of the Central Secretariat that I have not yet read."

sentences.zh: 」浚姑留之，他日試以文，乃大驚異。

translations.literal: " Jun kept him for the time being, and when he later tested him with a composition was greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: " Qiu Jun kept him for the time being, and when he later tested him with a composition was greatly astonished.

sentences.zh: 成化末，領京闈鄉試第一。

translations.literal: At the end of the Chenghua era he placed first in the Beijing provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Chenghua era he placed first in the Beijing provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 明年舉進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: The next year he passed the palace examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he passed the palace examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 益肆力古文，每有作，或據高樹，或閉坐一室，瞑目隱度，形容灰槁。

translations.literal: He devoted himself ever more fiercely to ancient prose. Whenever he set about composing, he would sometimes perch in a tall tree or shut himself alone in a room, close his eyes and inwardly measure his words, his face and form withered as ashes.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself ever more fiercely to ancient prose. Whenever he set about composing, he would sometimes perch in a tall tree or shut himself alone in a room, close his eyes and inwardly measure his words, his face and form withered as ashes.

sentences.zh: 自此文益奇，亦厚自負。

translations.literal: From then on his prose grew ever stranger, and Qi became deeply proud of himself.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his prose grew ever stranger, and Qi became deeply proud of himself.

sentences.zh: 尤尚節義。

translations.literal: He especially valued integrity and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He especially valued integrity and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 台諫救劉遜盡下獄，言當優容以全國體。

translations.literal: When censors and remonstrators who had rescued Liu Xun were all thrown into prison, Qi said they should be treated leniently to preserve the dignity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: When the censors and remonstrators who had rescued Liu Xun were all thrown into prison, Qi argued that they should be treated leniently to preserve the dignity of the state.

sentences.zh: 中官李廣死，遺一籍，具識大臣賄交者。

translations.literal: The eunuch Li Guang died and left behind a register fully recording which grand ministers had exchanged bribes with him.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Li Guang died, he left behind a register fully recording which grand ministers had exchanged bribes with him.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命言官指名劾奏。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged and ordered the remonstrating officials to impeach them by name.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and ordered the remonstrating officials to impeach them by name.

sentences.zh: 上言曰：「大臣表正百僚，今若此，固宜置重典。

translations.literal: Qi memorialized, saying, "Grand ministers set the standard for all officials. If matters stand as they do now, it is indeed fitting to impose heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Qi memorialized, saying, "Grand ministers set the standard for all officials. If matters stand as they do now, it is indeed fitting to impose heavy punishment.

sentences.zh: 然天下及四裔皆仰望之，一旦指名暴其惡，啟遠人慢朝廷心。

translations.literal: Yet all under Heaven and the four quarters look up to them; to expose their wickedness by name all at once would awaken in distant peoples a mind to slight the court.
translations.idiomatic: Yet all under Heaven and the four quarters look up to them; to expose their wickedness by name all at once would awaken in distant peoples a mind to slight the court.

sentences.zh: 言官未見籍記，憑臆而論，安辨玉石？

translations.literal: The remonstrators have not seen the register; to argue from speculation—how can they distinguish jade from stone?
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrators have not seen the register; to argue from speculation—how can they distinguish jade from stone?

sentences.zh: 一經攻摘，且玷終身。

translations.literal: Once attacked and exposed, their reputations would be stained for life.
translations.idiomatic: Once attacked and exposed, their reputations would be stained for life.

sentences.zh: 臣請降敕密諭，使引疾退，或斥以他事，庶不為朝廷羞，而仕路亦清。

translations.literal: Your servant asks that secret edicts be issued instructing them to plead illness and withdraw, or remove them on other grounds, so that the court may not be shamed and the path of office may also be cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant asks that secret edicts be issued instructing them to plead illness and withdraw, or remove them on other grounds, so that the court may not be shamed and the path of office may also be cleared.

sentences.zh: 」李夢陽下獄，言：「壽寧侯托肺腑，當有以保全之。

translations.literal: " When Li Mengyang was imprisoned, Qi said, "The Marquis of Shouning is the emperor's flesh and blood; he ought to have some means of preserving Mengyang.
translations.idiomatic: " When Li Mengyang was imprisoned, Qi said, "The Marquis of Shouning is the emperor's own kin; he ought to have some means of preserving Mengyang.

sentences.zh: 夢陽不保，為侯累。

translations.literal: If Mengyang is not preserved, it will implicate the marquis.
translations.idiomatic: If Mengyang is not preserved, it will implicate the marquis.

sentences.zh: 」帝深納焉。

translations.literal: " The emperor deeply accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor deeply accepted this.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，進侍讀。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was promoted to palace reader.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was promoted to palace reader.

sentences.zh: 正德初，遷南京太常少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhengde era he was transferred to vice minister of the Southern Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengde era he was transferred to vice minister of the Southern Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾亂政，李東陽依違其間。

translations.literal: Liu Jin threw government into disorder, and Li Dongyang wavered between alternatives.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin threw government into disorder, and Li Dongyang wavered between alternatives.

sentences.zh: ，東陽所舉士也，貽書責以大義，且請削門生之籍。

translations.literal: Qi, whom Dongyang had recommended, sent a letter rebuking him with the great principle at stake and asking to be struck from the roll of his disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, whom Li Dongyang had recommended, sent a letter rebuking him on the great principle at stake and asking to be struck from the roll of his disciples.

sentences.zh: 尋進本寺卿，擢南京吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to minister of that court and elevated to vice minister of the right in the Southern Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to minister of that court and elevated to vice minister of the right in the Southern Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 遇事嚴謹，僚屬畏憚。

translations.literal: In handling affairs he was strict and careful, and his colleagues feared him.
translations.idiomatic: In handling affairs he was strict and careful, and his colleagues feared him.

sentences.zh: 畿輔盜縱橫，而皇儲未建，疏論激切，且侵執政者。

translations.literal: Bandits ran rampant in the capital region, yet no heir had been established. Qi memorialized in heated language and even attacked those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits ran rampant in the capital region, yet no heir had been established. Qi memorialized in heated language and even attacked those in power.

sentences.zh: 七年冬，考績赴都，遂引疾致仕歸。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventh year he came to the capital for performance review, then pleaded illness, retired, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the seventh year he came to the capital for performance review, then pleaded illness, retired, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠慕其名，遣使饋，避之深山。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ning, Zhu Chenhao, admired his reputation and sent envoys with gifts; Qi avoided them by hiding deep in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ning, Zhu Chenhao, admired his reputation and sent envoys with gifts; Qi avoided them by hiding deep in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 及叛，已病，馳書守臣約討賊，事未舉而卒。

translations.literal: When the prince rebelled, Qi was already ill; he sent an urgent letter to the defending officials arranging to strike the rebels, but died before the plan could be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince rebelled, Qi was already ill; he sent an urgent letter to the defending officials arranging to strike the rebels, but died before the plan could be carried out.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，賜諡文肅，學者稱圭峰先生。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jiajing era he was granted the posthumous title Wensu, and scholars call him Master Guifeng.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jiajing era he was granted the posthumous title Wensu, and scholars call him Master Guifeng.

sentences.zh: 儲巏，字靜夫，泰州人。

translations.literal: Chu Guan, styled Jingfu, was a man of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Guan, styled Jingfu, came from Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 九歲能屬文。

translations.literal: At nine he could compose prose.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he could compose prose.

sentences.zh: 母疾，刲股療之，卒不起。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill he cut flesh from his thigh to treat her, but she still did not recover.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill he cut flesh from his thigh to treat her, but she still did not recover.

sentences.zh: 家貧，力營墓域。

translations.literal: The family was poor, yet he strained himself to prepare the burial ground.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor, yet he strained himself to prepare the burial ground.

sentences.zh: 旦哭冢，夜讀書不輟。

translations.literal: By day he wept at the tomb; by night he read without cease.
translations.idiomatic: By day he wept at the tomb; by night he read without cease.

sentences.zh: 成化十九年鄉試，明年會試，皆第一。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Chenghua he took the provincial examination, and the next year the metropolitan examination; in both he placed first.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Chenghua he took the provincial examination, and the next year the metropolitan examination; in both he placed first.

sentences.zh: 授南京考功主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief secretary in the Bureau of Evaluation at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief secretary in the Bureau of Evaluation at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嗣位，疏薦前直諫貶謫者，主事張吉、王純，中書舍人丁璣，進士李文祥，吉等皆錄用。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong succeeded, he memorialized recommending those who had remonstrated frankly and been demoted or exiled: chief secretaries Zhang Ji and Wang Chun, drafter Ding Ji, and presented scholar Li Wenxiang. Ji and the others were all appointed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong succeeded, he memorialized recommending those who had remonstrated frankly and been demoted or exiled: chief secretaries Zhang Ji and Wang Chun, drafter Ding Ji, and presented scholar Li Wenxiang. Ji and the others were all appointed.

sentences.zh: 久之，進郎中。

translations.literal: After a long time he was promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書耿裕知其賢，調北部，考注臧否，一齣至公。

translations.literal: Geng Yu, minister of personnel, knew his worth and transferred him to the northern directorate. In evaluating merit and demerit he was uniformly fair to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Geng Yu knew his worth and transferred him to the northern directorate. In evaluating merit and demerit he was utterly impartial.

sentences.zh: 嘗核實一官，裕欲改其評，巏正色曰：「公所執，何異王介甫！

translations.literal: Once when verifying the record of an official, Yu wanted to change Guan's assessment. Guan said sternly, "What you hold to—how is it different from Wang Jiepu!
translations.idiomatic: Once when verifying the record of an official, Yu wanted to change Guan's assessment. Guan said sternly, "What you hold to—how is it different from Wang Jiepu!

sentences.zh: 」群僚咸在側，裕大慚，徐曰：「郎中言是，然非我莫能容也。

translations.literal: " All the colleagues were present at his side. Yu was deeply ashamed and said slowly, "The director speaks rightly—yet no one but I could tolerate him.
translations.idiomatic: " All the colleagues were present at his side. Yu was deeply ashamed and said slowly, "The director speaks rightly—yet no one but I could tolerate him.

sentences.zh: 」擢太僕少卿，請命史官記注言動，如古左右史，時不能用。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Stud and requested that historiographers be ordered to record words and deeds, as in the ancient Left and Right Historiographers—but the proposal could not be adopted at the time.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Stud and requested that historiographers be ordered to record words and deeds, as in the ancient Left and Right Historiographers—but the proposal could not be adopted at the time.

sentences.zh: 進本寺卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to minister of that court.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of that court.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，塞上有警，條御邊五事，又陳馬政病民者四事，多議行。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong came to the throne, there was alarm on the northern frontier. He set forth five measures for defending the border and also submitted four points on how horse policy harmed the people; most were discussed and enacted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong came to the throne, there was alarm on the northern frontier. He set forth five measures for defending the border and also submitted four points on how horse policy harmed the people; most were discussed and enacted.

sentences.zh: 正德二年改左僉都御史，總督南京糧儲。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde he was made left censor-in-chief and put in overall charge of grain stores at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengde he was made left censor-in-chief and put in overall charge of grain stores at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 召為戶部右侍郎，尋轉左，督倉場，所至宿弊盡釐。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be vice minister of the right in the Ministry of Revenue, soon transferred to the left, and directed the granaries; wherever he went, long-standing abuses were entirely swept clean.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to be vice minister of the right in the Ministry of Revenue, soon transferred to the left, and directed the granaries; wherever he went, long-standing abuses were entirely swept clean.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾用事，數陵侮大臣，獨敬巏，稱為先生。

translations.literal: When Liu Jin held power he repeatedly insulted grand ministers, yet he alone respected Guan and called him Master.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin held power he repeatedly insulted grand ministers, yet he alone respected Guan and called him Master.

sentences.zh: 巏憤其所為，五年春，引疾求去。

translations.literal: Guan was outraged at Jin's conduct; in the spring of the fifth year he pleaded illness and asked to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was outraged at Jin's conduct; in the spring of the fifth year he pleaded illness and asked to leave office.

sentences.zh: 詔許乘傳，有司俟疾痊以聞。

translations.literal: An edict permitted him to travel by post relay; the responsible offices were to wait until his illness had healed and then report.
translations.idiomatic: An edict permitted him to travel by post relay; the responsible offices were to wait until his illness had healed and then report.

sentences.zh: 其秋，瑾敗，以故官召，辭不赴。

translations.literal: That autumn, when Jin fell, he was summoned to his former office but declined to go.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, when Jin fell, he was summoned to his former office but declined to go.

sentences.zh: 後起南京戶部左侍郎，就改吏部，卒官。

translations.literal: Later he was raised again as vice minister of the left in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, was then immediately transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was raised again as vice minister of the left in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, was then immediately transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 巏體貌清羸，若不勝衣；

translations.literal: Guan's build was slight and thin, as if his clothes were too heavy for him;
translations.idiomatic: Guan's build was slight and thin, as if his clothes were too heavy for him;

sentences.zh: 淳行清修，介然自守。

translations.literal: In conduct he was pure and self-cultivating, upright and self-restrained.
translations.idiomatic: In conduct he was pure and self-cultivating, upright and self-restrained.

sentences.zh: 工詩文。

translations.literal: He was skilled in poetry and prose.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in poetry and prose.

sentences.zh: 好推引知名士，辟遠非類，不惡而嚴。

translations.literal: He liked to recommend and advance famous scholars, kept his distance from unworthy sorts, and was not harsh yet severe.
translations.idiomatic: He liked to recommend and advance famous scholars, kept his distance from unworthy sorts, and was not harsh yet severe.

sentences.zh: 進士顧璘嘗謁尚書邵寶，寶語曰：「子立身，當以柴墟為法。

translations.literal: The presented scholar Gu Lin once called on Minister Shao Bao. Bao told him, "In establishing yourself, you should take Chai Xu as your model.
translations.idiomatic: The presented scholar Gu Lin once called on Minister Shao Bao. Bao told him, "In establishing yourself, you should take Chai Xu as your model.

sentences.zh: 」柴墟者，巏別號也。

translations.literal: " Chai Xu was Guan's sobriquet.
translations.idiomatic: " Chai Xu was Guan's sobriquet.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，賜諡文懿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jiajing era he was granted the posthumous title Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jiajing era he was granted the posthumous title Wenyi.
