sentences.zh: 李夢陽附 康海 王九思 王維楨

translations.literal: Li Mengyang with appended biographies: Kang Hai, Wang Jiusi, Wang Weizhen
translations.idiomatic: Li Mengyang with appended biographies: Kang Hai, Wang Jiusi, Wang Weizhen

sentences.zh: 李夢陽，字獻吉，慶陽人。

translations.literal: Li Mengyang, styled Xianji, was a man of Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mengyang, styled Xianji, came from Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 父正，官周王府教授，徙居開封。

translations.literal: His father Zheng served as instructor to the Prince of Zhou's household and moved the family to Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zheng served as instructor to the Prince of Zhou's household and moved the family to Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 母夢日墮懷而生，故名夢陽。

translations.literal: His mother dreamed that the sun fell into her bosom when she bore him, hence the name Mengyang.
translations.idiomatic: His mother dreamed that the sun fell into her bosom when she bore him, hence the name Mengyang.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年舉陝西鄉試第一，明年成進士，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongzhi he placed first in the Shaanxi provincial examination; the next year he passed the palace examination and was appointed secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Hongzhi he placed first in the Shaanxi provincial examination; the next year he passed the palace examination and was appointed secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 遷郎中，榷關，格勢要，構下獄，得釋。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director, served at the transit tax office, blocked powerful figures, was framed and imprisoned, and was released.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director, served at the transit tax office, blocked powerful figures, was framed and imprisoned, and was released.

sentences.zh: 十八年，應詔上書，陳二病、三害、六漸，凡五千余言，極論得失。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, responding to an imperial summons he submitted a memorial setting forth two maladies, three harms, and six gradual evils—more than five thousand words in all—arguing the rights and wrongs to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, responding to an imperial summons he submitted a memorial setting forth two maladies, three harms, and six gradual evils—more than five thousand words in all—arguing the rights and wrongs to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 末言：「壽寧侯張鶴齡招納無賴，罔利賊民，勢如翼虎。

translations.literal: At the end he wrote, "The Marquis of Shouning, Zhang Heling, gathers worthless men, pursues profit and wrongs the people, and his power is like a tiger with wings.
translations.idiomatic: At the end he wrote, "The Marquis of Shouning, Zhang Heling, gathers worthless men, pursues profit and wrongs the people, and his power is like a tiger with wings.

sentences.zh: 」鶴齡奏辨，摘疏中「陛下厚張氏」語，誣夢陽訕母后為張氏，罪當斬。

translations.literal: " Heling memorialized in his defense, seized on the phrase in the memorial "Your Majesty favors the Zhang clan," and falsely charged that Mengyang had slandered the empress dowager as belonging to the Zhang clan—a crime meriting decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: " Heling memorialized in his defense, seized on the phrase in the memorial "Your Majesty favors the Zhang clan," and falsely charged that Mengyang had slandered the empress dowager as belonging to the Zhang clan—a crime meriting decapitation.

sentences.zh: 時皇后有寵，後母金夫人泣訴帝，帝不得已系夢陽錦衣獄。

translations.literal: At the time the empress enjoyed favor, and her mother Lady Jin wept and appealed to the emperor. The emperor had no choice but to imprison Mengyang in the Brocade-Clad Guard prison.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the empress enjoyed favor, and her mother Lady Jin wept and appealed to the emperor. The emperor had no choice but to imprison Mengyang in the Brocade-Clad Guard prison.

sentences.zh: 尋宥出，奪俸。

translations.literal: Soon he was pardoned and released, but his salary was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was pardoned and released, but his salary was stripped.

sentences.zh: 金夫人訴不已，帝弗聽，召鶴齡閒處，切責之，鶴齡免冠叩頭乃已。

translations.literal: Lady Jin kept appealing without stop. The emperor would not listen, summoned Heling to a private setting, and sharply rebuked him; Heling removed his cap and knocked his head on the ground before the matter ended.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Jin kept appealing without stop. The emperor would not listen, summoned Heling to a private setting, and sharply rebuked him; Heling removed his cap and knocked his head on the ground before the matter ended.

sentences.zh: 左右知帝護夢陽，請毋重罪，而予杖以泄金夫人憤。

translations.literal: Those around the emperor knew he meant to protect Mengyang and asked that he not be heavily punished but instead be given the bastinado to vent Lady Jin's anger.
translations.idiomatic: Those around the emperor knew he meant to protect Mengyang and asked that he not be heavily punished but instead be given the bastinado to vent Lady Jin's anger.

sentences.zh: 帝又弗許，謂尚書劉大夏曰：「若輩欲以杖斃夢陽耳，吾寧殺直臣快左右心乎！

translations.literal: The emperor again refused and said to Minister Liu Daxia, "You people mean to beat Mengyang to death with the rod. Would I rather kill an upright minister to satisfy those around me!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again refused and said to Minister Liu Daxia, "You people mean to beat Mengyang to death with the rod. Would I rather kill an upright minister to satisfy those around me!

sentences.zh: 」他日，夢陽途遇壽寧侯，詈之，擊以馬箠，墮二齒，壽寧侯不敢校也。

translations.literal: " Another day Mengyang met the Marquis of Shouning on the road, cursed him, and struck him with a riding crop, knocking out two teeth; the marquis did not dare retaliate.
translations.idiomatic: " Another day Mengyang met the Marquis of Shouning on the road, cursed him, and struck him with a riding crop, knocking out two teeth; the marquis did not dare retaliate.

sentences.zh: 孝宗崩，武宗立，劉瑾等八虎用事，尚書韓文與其僚語及而泣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong died and Emperor Wuzong came to the throne, Liu Jin and the other Eight Tigers held power. Minister Han Wen spoke of it with his colleagues and wept.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong died and Emperor Wuzong came to the throne, Liu Jin and the other Eight Tigers held power. Minister Han Wen spoke of it with his colleagues and wept.

sentences.zh: 夢陽進曰：「公大臣，何泣也？

translations.literal: Mengyang stepped forward and said, "You are a grand minister—why weep?
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang stepped forward and said, "You are a grand minister—why weep?

sentences.zh: 」文曰：「奈何？

translations.literal: " Wen said, "What can be done?
translations.idiomatic: " Wen said, "What can be done?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「比言官劾群奄，閣臣持其章甚力，公誠率諸大臣伏闕爭，閣臣必應之，去若輩易耳。

translations.literal: " He said, "Just now the remonstrators impeached the eunuch clique, and the grand secretaries pressed their memorials hard. If you truly lead the grand ministers to prostrate yourselves at the palace gate in protest, the grand secretaries will surely respond—getting rid of people like them would be easy.
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "Just now the remonstrators impeached the eunuch clique, and the grand secretaries pressed their memorials hard. If you truly lead the grand ministers to prostrate yourselves at the palace gate in protest, the grand secretaries will surely respond—getting rid of people like them would be easy.

sentences.zh: 」文曰：「善」，屬夢陽屬草。

translations.literal: " Wen said, "Good," and charged Mengyang to draft the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " Wen said, "Good," and charged Mengyang to draft the memorial.

sentences.zh: 會語泄，文等皆逐去。

translations.literal: As it happened the plan leaked, and Wen and the others were all driven out.
translations.idiomatic: As it happened the plan leaked, and Wen and the others were all driven out.

sentences.zh: 瑾深憾之，矯旨謫山西布政司經歷，勒致仕。

translations.literal: Jin deeply resented this, forged an edict banishing him to be administrator of the Shanxi provincial administration commission, and compelled him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Jin deeply resented this, forged an edict banishing him to be administrator of the Shanxi provincial administration commission, and compelled him to retire.

sentences.zh: 既而瑾復摭他事下夢陽獄，將殺之，康海為說瑾，乃免。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Jin again seized on other matters and had Mengyang thrown into prison, intending to kill him; Kang Hai pleaded with Jin on his behalf, and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Jin again seized on other matters and had Mengyang thrown into prison, intending to kill him; Kang Hai pleaded with Jin on his behalf, and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，起故官，遷江西提學副使。

translations.literal: After Jin was executed he was raised to his former office and transferred to vice commissioner for education in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed he was raised to his former office and transferred to vice commissioner for education in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 令甲，副使屬總督，夢陽與相抗，總督陳金惡之。

translations.literal: By regulation a vice commissioner was subordinate to the grand coordinator; Mengyang resisted this, and Grand Coordinator Chen Jin hated him.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation a vice commissioner was subordinate to the grand coordinator; Mengyang resisted this, and Grand Coordinator Chen Jin hated him.

sentences.zh: 監司五日會揖巡按御史，夢陽又不往揖，且敕諸生毋謁上官，即謁，長揖毋跪。

translations.literal: Every five days the surveillance commissioners were to gather and bow to the touring censor; Mengyang again would not go to bow. He also instructed the students not to call on superiors; if they did call, they were to make a long bow and not kneel.
translations.idiomatic: Every five days the surveillance commissioners were to gather and bow to the touring censor; Mengyang again would not go to bow. He also instructed the students not to call on superiors; if they did call, they were to make a long bow and not kneel.

sentences.zh: 御史江萬實亦惡夢陽。

translations.literal: Censor Jiang Wanshi also hated Mengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Jiang Wanshi also hated Mengyang.

sentences.zh: 淮王府校與諸生爭，夢陽笞校。

translations.literal: Retainers of the Prince of Huai's household quarreled with students, and Mengyang had the retainers beaten with the bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Retainers of the Prince of Huai's household quarreled with students, and Mengyang had the retainers beaten with the bamboo.

sentences.zh: 王怒，奏之，下御史按治。

translations.literal: The prince was enraged, memorialized about it, and the censor was sent down to investigate and punish.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was enraged, memorialized about it, and the censor was sent down to investigate and punish.

sentences.zh: 夢陽恐萬實右王，訐萬實。

translations.literal: Mengyang feared Wanshi would favor the prince and impeached Wanshi.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang feared Wanshi would favor the prince and impeached Wanshi.

sentences.zh: 詔下總督金行勘，金檄布政使鄭岳勘之。

translations.literal: An edict was issued ordering Grand Coordinator Jin to conduct an investigation; Jin dispatched a command to Provincial Administration Commissioner Zheng Yue to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Grand Coordinator Jin to investigate the matter; Jin in turn dispatched Provincial Administration Commissioner Zheng Yue to conduct the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 夢陽偽撰萬實劾金疏以激怒金，並構岳子涷通賄事。

translations.literal: Mengyang forged a memorial from Wanshi impeaching Jin to enrage Jin, and also fabricated a matter implicating Yue's son Dong in taking bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang forged a memorial in Wanshi's name impeaching Jin in order to enrage him, and also fabricated charges that Yue's son Dong had accepted bribes.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠者浮慕夢陽，嘗請撰《陽春書院記》，又惡岳，乃助夢陽劾岳。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ning, Chen Hao, superficially admired Mengyang, once asked him to compose 《Record of the Yangchun Academy》, also hated Yue, and so helped Mengyang impeach Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ning, Chen Hao, professed admiration for Mengyang and once asked him to write 《Record of the Yangchun Academy》; he also hated Yue and therefore helped Mengyang impeach him.

sentences.zh: 萬實復奏夢陽短，及偽為奏章事。

translations.literal: Wanshi memorialized again about Mengyang's faults and about the matter of forging memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Wanshi memorialized again, citing Mengyang's faults and the matter of the forged memorial.

sentences.zh: 參政吳廷舉亦與夢陽有隙，上疏論其侵官，不俟命徑去。

translations.literal: Administrative Vice Commissioner Wu Tingju also had a rift with Mengyang; he memorialized about Mengyang's overstepping his office and left directly without awaiting orders.
translations.idiomatic: Administrative Vice Commissioner Wu Tingju also had a grievance against Mengyang; he memorialized that Mengyang had overstepped his authority and left his post without awaiting orders.

sentences.zh: 詔遣大理卿燕忠往鞫，召夢陽，羈廣信獄。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Minister of Justice Yan Zhong to conduct the inquest, summoned Mengyang, and detained him in Guangxin prison.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Minister of Justice Yan Zhong to conduct the inquest, summoned Mengyang, and held him in Guangxin prison.

sentences.zh: 諸生萬余為訟冤，不聽。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand students petitioned on his behalf; the court would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand students petitioned on his behalf, but the court refused to hear them.

sentences.zh: 劾夢陽陵轢同列，挾制上官，遂以冠帶閒住去。

translations.literal: Mengyang was impeached for trampling upon colleagues and coercing superiors; he was then dismissed to reside at home while retaining cap and belt.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang was impeached for riding roughshod over colleagues and coercing his superiors, and was dismissed to live at home while retaining honorary rank.

sentences.zh: 亦褫岳職，謫戍澐，奪廷舉俸。

translations.literal: Yue's office was also stripped; he was banished to garrison duty at Yun; Tingju's salary was taken away.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was also stripped of office and banished to military service at Yun, and Tingju's salary was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 夢陽既家居，益跅弛負氣，治園池，招賓客，日縱俠少射獵繁台、晉丘間，自號空同子，名震海內。

translations.literal: Once Mengyang was living at home, he became even more unrestrained and defiant in spirit; he laid out gardens and ponds, invited guests, and every day let gallant youths hunt with him between Fantai and Jinqiu; he styled himself Master Kongtong, and his fame shook the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Once Mengyang was living at home, he grew even more unrestrained and proud; he laid out gardens and ponds, entertained guests, and every day led gallant youths in hunting between Fantai and Jinqiu. He styled himself Master Kongtong, and his fame resounded throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 宸濠反誅，御史周宣劾夢陽黨逆，被逮。

translations.literal: After Chen Hao's rebellion was suppressed and he was executed, Censor Zhou Xuan impeached Mengyang as a rebel partisan, and he was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen Hao's rebellion was crushed and he was executed, Censor Zhou Xuan impeached Mengyang as a rebel sympathizer, and he was arrested.

sentences.zh: 大學士楊廷和、尚書林俊力救之，坐前作《書院記》，削籍。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Yang Tinghe and Minister Lin Jun vigorously pleaded for him; for his earlier composition of 《Record of the Academy》, he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Yang Tinghe and Minister Lin Jun pleaded vigorously for him, but for having earlier written 《Record of the Academy》, he was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 頃之卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 子枝，進士。

translations.literal: His son Zhi became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi became a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 夢陽才思雄鷙，卓然以復古自命。

translations.literal: Mengyang's literary talent was bold and fierce; he conspicuously styled himself a restorer of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang's literary talent was bold and fierce; he conspicuously styled himself a restorer of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 弘治時，宰相李東陽主文柄，天下翕然宗之，夢陽獨譏其萎弱。

translations.literal: During the Hongzhi reign, Chancellor Li Dongyang held sway over literature, and the realm all looked to him as their model; Mengyang alone mocked his feebleness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign, Chancellor Li Dongyang held sway over literature and the realm looked to him as its model; Mengyang alone mocked his feebleness.

sentences.zh: 倡言文必秦、漢，詩必盛唐，非是者弗道。

translations.literal: He proclaimed that prose must follow Qin and Han, poetry must follow the High Tang—anything else he would not speak of.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed that prose must follow Qin and Han and poetry the High Tang; anything else he would not discuss.

sentences.zh: 與何景明、徐禎卿、邊貢、朱應登、顧璘、陳沂、鄭善夫、康海、王九思等號十才子，又與景明、禎卿、貢、海、九思、王廷相號七才子，皆卑視一世，而夢陽尤甚。

translations.literal: With He Jingming, Xu Zhenqing, Bian Gong, Zhu Yingdeng, Gu Lin, Chen Yi, Zheng Shanfu, Kang Hai, Wang Jiusi, and others he was styled the Ten Talents; with Jingming, Zhenqing, Gong, Hai, Jiusi, and Wang Tingxiang he was also styled the Seven Talents—they all looked down on their age, but Mengyang especially so.
translations.idiomatic: With He Jingming, Xu Zhenqing, Bian Gong, Zhu Yingdeng, Gu Lin, Chen Yi, Zheng Shanfu, Kang Hai, Wang Jiusi, and others he was known as one of the Ten Talents; with Jingming, Zhenqing, Gong, Hai, Jiusi, and Wang Tingxiang he was also called one of the Seven Talents. They all looked down on their age, but Mengyang most of all.

sentences.zh: 吳人黃省曾、越人周祚，千里致書，願為弟子。

translations.literal: Huang Shengzeng of Wu and Zhou Zuo of Yue sent letters from a thousand li away, wishing to become his disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Shengzeng of Wu and Zhou Zuo of Yue sent letters from a thousand li away, asking to become his disciples.

sentences.zh: 迨嘉靖朝，李攀龍、王世貞出，復奉以為宗。

translations.literal: By the Jiajing reign, when Li Panlong and Wang Shizhen arose, they again revered him as their master.
translations.idiomatic: By the Jiajing reign, when Li Panlong and Wang Shizhen came to prominence, they again revered him as their master.

sentences.zh: 天下推李、何、王、李為四大家，無不爭效其體。

translations.literal: The realm acclaimed Li, He, Wang, and Li as the Four Great Masters, and all strove to imitate their style.
translations.idiomatic: The realm acclaimed Li, He, Wang, and Li as the Four Great Masters, and all strove to imitate their style.

sentences.zh: 華州王維楨以為七言律自杜甫以後，善用頓挫倒插之法，惟夢陽一人。

translations.literal: Wang Weizhen of Huazhou held that since Du Fu, in regulated verse in seven-character lines only Mengyang had mastered the use of abrupt turns and inverted insertions.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Weizhen of Huazhou held that since Du Fu, only Mengyang had mastered abrupt turns and inverted insertions in seven-character regulated verse.

sentences.zh: 而後有譏夢陽詩文者，則謂其模擬剽竊，得史遷、少陵之似，而失其真雲。

translations.literal: Yet later critics of Mengyang's poetry and prose said he imitated and plagiarized—he attained resemblance to Sima Qian and Du Fu but lost their truth, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Yet later critics of Mengyang's poetry and prose said he merely imitated and plagiarized: he achieved the likeness of Sima Qian and Du Fu but lost their essence, or so they said.

sentences.zh: 康海，字德涵，武功人。

translations.literal: Kang Hai, styled Dehan, was a native of Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Hai, styled Dehan, was a native of Wugong.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年殿試第一，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Hongzhi he ranked first in the palace examination and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Hongzhi he ranked first in the palace examination and was appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 與夢陽輩相倡和，訾議諸先達，忌者頗眾。

translations.literal: He exchanged poems with Mengyang and his circle, criticized the senior masters, and had many who resented him.
translations.idiomatic: He exchanged poems with Mengyang and his circle, criticized the senior masters, and made many enemies.

sentences.zh: 正德初，劉瑾亂政。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhengde reign, Liu Jin threw the government into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengde reign, Liu Jin threw the government into disorder.

sentences.zh: 以海同鄉，慕其才，欲招致之，海不肯往。

translations.literal: Because Hai was from the same native place, Jin admired his talent and wished to win him over, but Hai refused to go.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hai was a fellow townsman, Jin admired his talent and wished to win him over, but Hai refused to go.

sentences.zh: 會夢陽下獄，書片紙招海曰：「對山救我。

translations.literal: When Mengyang was thrown into prison, he wrote on a slip of paper summoning Hai, saying, "Duishan, save me."
translations.idiomatic: When Mengyang was thrown into prison, he wrote on a slip of paper summoning Hai, saying, "Duishan, save me."

sentences.zh: 」對山者，海別號也。

translations.literal: " Duishan was Hai's alternate style name.
translations.idiomatic: " Duishan was Hai's alternate style name.

sentences.zh: 海乃謁瑾，瑾大喜，為倒屣迎。

translations.literal: Hai then called on Jin; Jin was overjoyed and went out with slippers reversed to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Hai then called on Jin; Jin was overjoyed and went out with slippers reversed to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 海因設詭辭說之，瑾意解，明日釋夢陽。

translations.literal: Hai thereupon used devious words to persuade him; Jin's mind was eased, and the next day Mengyang was released.
translations.idiomatic: Hai thereupon used devious words to persuade him; Jin's mind was eased, and the next day Mengyang was released.

sentences.zh: 逾年，瑾敗，海坐黨，落職。

translations.literal: A year later Jin fell; Hai was punished as a partisan and lost his office.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Jin fell; Hai was punished as a partisan and lost his office.

sentences.zh: 王九思，字敬夫，鄠人。

translations.literal: Wang Jiusi, styled Jingfu, was a native of Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiusi, styled Jingfu, was a native of Hu.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the ninth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the ninth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士授檢討。

translations.literal: From Hanlin bachelor he was appointed Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: From Hanlin bachelor he was appointed Reviser.

sentences.zh: 尋調吏部，至郎中，亦以瑾黨謫壽州同知。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, rose to bureau director, and was also demoted to assistant prefect of Shouzhou as a member of Jin's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, rose to bureau director, and was also demoted to assistant prefect of Shouzhou as a member of Jin's faction.

sentences.zh: 復被論，勒致仕。

translations.literal: He was impeached again and compelled to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached again and compelled to retire.

sentences.zh: 海、九思同里、同官，同以瑾黨廢。

translations.literal: Hai and Jiusi were from the same place and held the same offices; both were dismissed as members of Jin's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Hai and Jiusi were from the same place and held the same offices; both were dismissed as members of Jin's faction.

sentences.zh: 每相聚沜東鄠、杜間，挾聲伎酣飲，制樂造歌曲，自比俳優，以寄其怫郁。

translations.literal: They often gathered between the Fen River east of Hu and Du, brought singing girls and drank freely, composed music and wrote songs, likened themselves to comic performers, and so gave vent to their resentment.
translations.idiomatic: They often gathered between the Fen River east of Hu and Du, brought singing girls and drank freely, composed music and wrote songs, likened themselves to comic performers, and so gave vent to their resentment.

sentences.zh: 九思嘗費重貲購樂工學琵琶。

translations.literal: Jiusi once spent a large sum to buy a musician and learn the pipa.
translations.idiomatic: Jiusi once spent a large sum to buy a musician and learn the pipa.

sentences.zh: 海搊彈尤善。

translations.literal: Hai was especially skilled at strumming and playing.
translations.idiomatic: Hai was especially skilled at strumming and playing.

sentences.zh: 後人傳相仿效，大雅之道微矣。

translations.literal: Later generations spread the tale and imitated them, and the way of high refinement declined.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations spread the tale and imitated them, and the way of high refinement declined.

sentences.zh: 王維楨，字允寧。

translations.literal: Wang Weizhen, styled Yunning.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Weizhen, styled Yunning.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十四年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fourteenth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the fourteenth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 擢庶吉士，累官南京國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was selected as Hanlin bachelor and by successive promotions became chancellor of the National University at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as Hanlin bachelor and by successive promotions became chancellor of the National University at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 家居，地大震，壓死。

translations.literal: While living at home, a great earthquake occurred and he was crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: While living at home, a great earthquake occurred and he was crushed to death.

sentences.zh: 維楨頎而晰，自負經世才，職文墨，不得少效於世，使酒謾罵，人多畏而遠之。

translations.literal: Weizhen was tall and fair-skinned; he fancied himself talented for statecraft but served in literary posts and could achieve little in the world; he drank and reviled others freely, and most people feared him and kept their distance.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhen was tall and fair-skinned; he fancied himself talented for statecraft but served in literary posts and could achieve little in the world. He drank and reviled others freely, and most people feared him and kept their distance.

sentences.zh: 於文好司馬遷，於詩好杜甫，而其意以夢陽兼此二人。

translations.literal: In prose he favored Sima Qian, in poetry Du Fu, but in his mind he held that Mengyang combined both men.
translations.idiomatic: In prose he favored Sima Qian and in poetry Du Fu, but in his mind Mengyang combined both.

sentences.zh: 終身所服膺效法者，夢陽也。

translations.literal: The man he revered and emulated all his life was Mengyang.
translations.idiomatic: The man he revered and emulated all his life was Mengyang.

sentences.zh: 何景明

translations.literal: He Jingming
translations.idiomatic: He Jingming

sentences.zh: 何景明，字仲默，信陽人。

translations.literal: He Jingming, styled Zhongmo, was a native of Xinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He Jingming, styled Zhongmo, was a native of Xinyang.

sentences.zh: 八歲能詩古文。

translations.literal: At eight he could compose poetry and ancient-style prose.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he could compose poetry and ancient-style prose.

sentences.zh: 弘治十一年舉於鄉，年方十五，宗籓貴人爭遺人負視，所至聚觀若堵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Hongzhi he passed the provincial examination at only fifteen; princes and nobles of the imperial clans vied to send people to carry him in palanquins to see him, and wherever he went crowds gathered to watch as thick as a wall.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Hongzhi he passed the provincial examination at only fifteen. Princes and nobles of the imperial clans vied to send men to carry him in palanquins to see him, and wherever he went crowds gathered as thick as a wall.

sentences.zh: 十五年第進士，授中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he ranked as jinshi and was appointed Secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he ranked as jinshi and was appointed Secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 與李夢陽輩倡詩古文，夢陽最雄駿，景明稍後出，相與頡頏。

translations.literal: He promoted ancient-style poetry and prose with Li Mengyang and his circle; Mengyang was the boldest and most forceful, Jingming came slightly later, and they matched each other in rivalry.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted ancient-style poetry and prose with Li Mengyang and his circle. Mengyang was the boldest and most forceful; Jingming came slightly later, and the two matched each other in rivalry.

sentences.zh: 正德改元，劉瑾竊柄。

translations.literal: When the Zhengde reign began, Liu Jin usurped power.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhengde reign began, Liu Jin usurped power.

sentences.zh: 上書吏部尚書許進勸其秉政毋撓，語極激烈。

translations.literal: He wrote to Minister of Personnel Xu Jin urging him to hold firm in government and not yield; his language was extremely fierce.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Minister of Personnel Xu Jin urging him to hold firm in government and not yield; his language was extremely fierce.

sentences.zh: 已，遂謝病歸。

translations.literal: Presently he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Presently he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 逾年，瑾盡免諸在告者官，景明坐罷。

translations.literal: A year later Jin dismissed all who were on sick leave from office; Jingming was consequently removed.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Jin dismissed all who were on sick leave from office; Jingming was consequently removed.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，用李東陽薦，起故秩，直內閣制敕房。

translations.literal: After Jin was executed, on Li Dongyang's recommendation he was restored to his former rank and served in the Grand Secretariat's Edict Drafting Office.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed, on Li Dongyang's recommendation he was restored to his former rank and served in the Grand Secretariat's Edict Drafting Office.

sentences.zh: 李夢陽下獄，眾莫敢為直，景明上書吏部尚書楊一清救之。

translations.literal: When Li Mengyang was thrown into prison, none dared speak for him; Jingming wrote to Minister of Personnel Yang Yiqing to save him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mengyang was thrown into prison, none dared speak for him; Jingming wrote to Minister of Personnel Yang Yiqing to save him.

sentences.zh: 九年，乾清宮災，疏言義子不當畜，邊軍不當留，番僧不當寵，宦官不當任。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when the Qianqing Palace burned, he memorialized that honorary sons should not be kept, frontier troops should not be retained, Tibetan monks should not be favored, and eunuchs should not be entrusted with office.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when the Qianqing Palace burned, he memorialized that honorary sons should not be kept, frontier troops should not be retained, Tibetan monks should not be favored, and eunuchs should not be entrusted with office.

sentences.zh: 留中。

translations.literal: The memorial was kept at court without action.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was kept at court without action.

sentences.zh: 久之，進吏部員外郎，直制敕如故。

translations.literal: After a long while he was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Personnel, continuing his service in the Edict Drafting Office as before.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Personnel, continuing his service in the Edict Drafting Office as before.

sentences.zh: 錢寧欲交歡，以古畫索題，景明曰：「此名筆，毋污人手。

translations.literal: Qian Ning wished to befriend him and asked him to inscribe an ancient painting; Jingming said, "This is the brushwork of a master—do not let it be soiled by human hands."
translations.idiomatic: Qian Ning wished to befriend him and asked him to inscribe an ancient painting; Jingming said, "This is the brushwork of a master—do not let it be soiled by human hands."

sentences.zh: 」留經年，終擲還之。

translations.literal: " He kept it for nearly a year and finally threw it back at him.
translations.idiomatic: " He kept it for nearly a year and finally threw it back at him.

sentences.zh: 尋擢陝西提學副使。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to vice commissioner for education in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to vice commissioner for education in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 廖鵬弟太監鑾鎮關中，橫甚，諸參隨遇三司不下馬，景明執撻之。

translations.literal: Liao Bin's younger brother, the eunuch Luan, garrisoned Guanzhong and was extremely overbearing; when visiting commissioners of the three offices encountered him they did not dismount; Jingming seized a whip and beat him.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Bin's younger brother, the eunuch Luan, garrisoned Guanzhong and was extremely overbearing; when visiting commissioners of the three offices encountered him they did not dismount, but Jingming seized a whip and beat him.

sentences.zh: 其教諸生，專以經術世務。

translations.literal: In instructing students he focused on classical learning and practical affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: In instructing students he focused on classical learning and practical affairs of the age.

sentences.zh: 遴秀者於正學書院，親為說經，不用諸家訓詁，士始知有經學。

translations.literal: He selected outstanding ones at the Academy of Correct Learning and personally expounded the classics, not using the exegetical glosses of various schools; scholars then first came to know that there was classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: He selected outstanding students at the Academy of Correct Learning and personally expounded the classics without relying on the exegetical glosses of various schools; scholars then first came to know what classical learning was.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，引疾歸，未幾卒，年三十有九。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he cited illness and returned home; before long he died, aged thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jiajing he cited illness and returned home; before long he died, aged thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 景明志操耿介，尚節義，鄙榮利，與夢陽並有國士風。

translations.literal: Jingming's integrity was upright and unyielding; he honored integrity and righteousness and despised honor and profit; he and Mengyang both had the bearing of men of national stature.
translations.idiomatic: Jingming's integrity was upright and unyielding; he honored integrity and righteousness and despised honor and profit. He and Mengyang both had the bearing of men of national stature.

sentences.zh: 兩人為詩文，初相得甚歡，名成之後，互相詆諆。

translations.literal: The two in poetry and prose at first got on very well; after their fame was established they slandered each other.
translations.idiomatic: The two in poetry and prose at first got on very well; after their fame was established they slandered each other.

sentences.zh: 夢陽主摹仿，景明則主創造，各樹堅壘不相下，兩人交游亦遂分左右袒。

translations.literal: Mengyang championed imitation, while Jingming championed creation; each built firm ramparts and would not yield, and their associates likewise took sides.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang championed imitation while Jingming championed creation; each built firm ramparts and would not yield, and their associates likewise took sides.

sentences.zh: 說者謂景明之才本遜夢陽，而其詩秀逸穩稱，視夢陽反為過之。

translations.literal: Commentators said Jingming's talent was originally inferior to Mengyang's, yet his poetry was elegant, effortless, and well-balanced—regarded alongside Mengyang he was actually superior.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators said Jingming's talent was originally inferior to Mengyang's, yet his poetry was elegant, effortless, and well-balanced—regarded alongside Mengyang he was actually superior.

sentences.zh: 然天下語詩文必並稱何、李，又與邊貢、徐禎卿並稱四傑。

translations.literal: Yet when the realm spoke of poetry and prose they always paired He and Li, and he was also paired with Bian Gong and Xu Zhenqing as the Four Outstanding Talents.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the realm spoke of poetry and prose they always paired He and Li, and he was also paired with Bian Gong and Xu Zhenqing as the Four Outstanding Talents.

sentences.zh: 其持論，謂：「詩溺於陶，謝力振之，古詩之法亡於謝。

translations.literal: His doctrine held: "Poetry sank into Tao; Xie strove to revive it—the ancient method of poetry perished with Xie.
translations.idiomatic: His doctrine held: "Poetry sank into Tao; Xie strove to revive it—the ancient method of poetry perished with Xie.

sentences.zh: 文靡於隋，韓力振之，古文之法亡於韓。

translations.literal: Prose grew decadent in the Sui; Han strove to revive it—the ancient method of prose perished with Han.
translations.idiomatic: Prose grew decadent in the Sui; Han strove to revive it—the ancient method of prose perished with Han.

sentences.zh: 」錢謙益撰《列朝詩》，力詆之。

translations.literal: " Qian Qianyi compiled 《Poetry of Successive Dynasties》 and fiercely denounced him.
translations.idiomatic: " Qian Qianyi compiled 《Poetry of Successive Dynasties》 and fiercely denounced him.

sentences.zh: 徐禎卿

translations.literal: Xu Zhenqing
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhenqing

sentences.zh: （楊循吉 祝允明 唐寅 桑悅）〉

translations.literal: (Yang Xunji, Zhu Yunming, Tang Yin, Sang Yue)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Yang Xunji, Zhu Yunming, Tang Yin, and Sang Yue)〉

sentences.zh: 徐禎卿，字昌榖，吳縣人。

translations.literal: Xu Zhenqing, styled Changgu, was a native of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhenqing, styled Changgu, was a native of Wu County.

sentences.zh: 資穎特，家不蓄一書，而無所不通。

translations.literal: His endowment was exceptionally sharp; his household kept not a single book, yet there was nothing he did not know.
translations.idiomatic: His endowment was exceptionally sharp; his household kept not a single book, yet there was nothing he did not know.

sentences.zh: 自為諸生，已工詩歌，與裡人唐寅善，寅言之沈周、楊循吉，由是知名。

translations.literal: Even as a student he was already skilled in poetry and song; he was friendly with his fellow townsman Tang Yin, and when Yin spoke of him to Shen Zhou and Yang Xunji, he thereby became known.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a student he was already skilled in poetry and song. He was friendly with his fellow townsman Tang Yin, and when Yin spoke of him to Shen Zhou and Yang Xunji, he thereby became known.

sentences.zh: 舉弘治十八年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighteenth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 孝宗遣中使問禎卿與華亭陸深名，深遂得館選，而禎卿以貌寢不與。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong sent a palace messenger to ask after the names of Zhenqing and Lu Shen of Huating; Shen thereupon gained selection for the Hanlin, but Zhenqing because of his uncomely appearance was not included.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong sent a palace messenger to ask after the names of Zhenqing and Lu Shen of Huating; Shen thereupon gained Hanlin selection, but Zhenqing because of his uncomely appearance was not included.

sentences.zh: 授大理左寺副，坐失囚，貶國子博士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Vice Director of the Court of Review; for losing a prisoner he was demoted to Doctor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Left Vice Director of the Court of Review; for losing a prisoner he was demoted to Doctor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 禎卿少與祝允明、唐寅、文徵明齊名，號「吳中四才子」。

translations.literal: In youth Zhenqing was equally famous with Zhu Yunming, Tang Yin, and Wen Zhengming, and they were styled the "Four Talents of Wu."
translations.idiomatic: In youth Zhenqing was equally famous with Zhu Yunming, Tang Yin, and Wen Zhengming, and they were known as the "Four Talents of Wu."

sentences.zh: 其為讀，喜白居易、劉禹錫。

translations.literal: In his reading he favored Bai Juyi and Liu Yuxi.
translations.idiomatic: In his reading he favored Bai Juyi and Liu Yuxi.

sentences.zh: 既登第，與李夢陽、何景明游，悔其少作，改而趨漢、魏、盛唐，然故習猶在，夢陽譏其守而未化。

translations.literal: After passing the examinations he associated with Li Mengyang and He Jingming, regretted his youthful work, and turned toward Han, Wei, and the High Tang; yet old habits remained, and Mengyang mocked him for holding fast without being transformed.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the examinations he associated with Li Mengyang and He Jingming, regretted his youthful work, and turned toward Han, Wei, and the High Tang; yet old habits remained, and Mengyang mocked him for holding fast without being transformed.

sentences.zh: 卒，年二十有三。

translations.literal: He died, aged twenty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died, aged twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 禎卿體癯神清，詩熔煉精警，為吳中詩人之冠，年雖不永，名滿士林。

translations.literal: Zhenqing was gaunt in body and clear in spirit; his poetry was smelted and refined, sharp and alert; he was foremost among Wu poets; though his years were not long, his fame filled the world of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing was gaunt in body and clear in spirit; his poetry was smelted and refined, sharp and alert. He was foremost among Wu poets; though his years were not long, his fame filled the world of scholars.

sentences.zh: 子伯虯，舉人，亦能詩。

translations.literal: His son Bohao became a provincial graduate and could also compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bohao became a provincial graduate and could also compose poetry.

sentences.zh: 楊循吉，字君謙，吳縣人。

translations.literal: Yang Xunji, styled Junqian, was a native of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xunji, styled Junqian, was a native of Wu County.

sentences.zh: 成化二十年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the twentieth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the twentieth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 授禮部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 善病，好讀書，每得意，手足踔掉不能自禁，用是得顛主事名。

translations.literal: He was often ill and loved reading; whenever he was pleased with himself his hands and feet would leap and dance beyond his control; for this he got the nickname "Mad Clerk."
translations.idiomatic: He was often ill and loved reading; whenever he was pleased with himself his hands and feet would leap and dance beyond his control, and for this he earned the nickname "Mad Clerk."

sentences.zh: 一歲中，數移病不出。

translations.literal: In the course of a year he several times took sick leave and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: In the course of a year he several times took sick leave and did not go out.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，奏乞改教，不許。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi he memorialized asking to change his teaching post; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongzhi reign he petitioned to be transferred to an instructorship, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 遂請致仕歸，年才三十有一。

translations.literal: He then requested retirement and returned home, his age being only thirty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to retire and go home, though he was only thirty-one.

sentences.zh: 結廬支硎山下，課讀經史，旁通內典、稗官。

translations.literal: He built a hut below Mount Zhixie, set himself to reading the classics and histories, and also mastered Buddhist scriptures and unofficial histories.
translations.idiomatic: He built a cottage at the foot of Mount Zhixie, devoted himself to the classics and histories, and also ranged widely through Buddhist texts and popular tales.

sentences.zh: 父母歿，傾貲治葬，寢苫墓側。

translations.literal: When his parents died he spent all his property on their burial and slept on mourning mats beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: After his parents died he poured out his fortune on their funeral and kept vigil on straw mats beside the grave.

sentences.zh: 性狷隘，好持人短長，又好以學問窮人，至頰赤不顧。

translations.literal: By nature he was narrow and petty, fond of airing others' faults and shortcomings, and also fond of using learning to corner people in debate, not caring even when cheeks flushed red.
translations.idiomatic: He was narrow-minded by nature, loved to dwell on others' faults, and delighted in trapping people with erudite argument, heedless even when faces turned crimson.

sentences.zh: 清寧宮災，詔求直言，馳疏請復建文帝尊號，格不行。

translations.literal: When the Qingning Palace burned, an edict sought frank counsel; he sent a memorial in haste asking that the posthumous title of the Jianwen Emperor be restored, but it was blocked and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: After fire destroyed the Qingning Palace, the throne called for blunt counsel; he rushed off a memorial urging restoration of the Jianwen Emperor's honorific title, but the proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 武宗駐蹕南都，召賦《打虎曲》，稱旨，易武人裝，日侍御前為樂府、小令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong halted at the Southern Capital he was summoned to compose 《Tiger-beating Song》; it pleased the Emperor; he changed into military dress and daily waited before the throne composing yuefu and short songs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong sojourned at the Southern Capital, he was called to write 《Tiger-beating Song》; the piece pleased the throne, and he donned martial garb, serving daily at court to compose yuefu lyrics and short tunes.

sentences.zh: 帝以優俳畜之，不授官。

translations.literal: The Emperor kept him as an actor and entertainer and did not grant him office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor treated him as a court performer and gave him no official post.

sentences.zh: 循吉以為恥，閱九月辭歸。

translations.literal: Xunji regarded this as a disgrace; after nine months he resigned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Xunji took this as a humiliation and, nine months later, resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 既復召至京，會帝崩，乃還。

translations.literal: He was soon summoned back to the capital again, but as the Emperor died he then returned.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital again, but the Emperor died before matters could proceed, and he returned home.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，獻《九廟頌》及《華陽求嗣齋儀》，報聞而已。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing era he presented 《Ode to the Nine Temples》 and 《Rites of the Huayang Hall for Seeking an Heir》; acknowledgment was noted, and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign he submitted 《Ode to the Nine Temples》 and 《Rites of the Huayang Hall for Praying for an Heir》, but received only routine acknowledgment.

sentences.zh: 晚歲落寞，益堅癖自好。

translations.literal: In his later years he was desolate; he grew ever more firmly eccentric in his personal tastes.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he lived in lonely decline and clung ever more stubbornly to his eccentric ways.

sentences.zh: 尚書顧璘道吳，以幣贄，促膝論文，歡甚。

translations.literal: Minister Gu Lin was passing through Wu; Xunji brought gifts of silk and, sitting knee to knee, discussed literature with great delight.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Gu Lin traveled through Wu, Xunji brought him gifts of silk; they sat close together discussing literature and were exceedingly happy.

sentences.zh: 俄郡守邀璘，璘將赴之，循吉忽色變，驅之出，擲還其幣。

translations.literal: Soon the prefect invited Lin; as Lin was about to go, Xunji suddenly changed color, drove him out, and threw back his gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the prefect invited Lin, and as Lin was about to accept, Xunji's face darkened; he drove Lin out and hurled back the gifts.

sentences.zh: 明日，璘往謝，閉門不納。

translations.literal: The next day Lin went to apologize; the door was closed and he was not admitted.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Lin came to apologize, but Xunji shut his door and refused him entry.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十九。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-nine.

sentences.zh: 其詩文，自定為《松籌堂集》，他所作又十余種，幾及千卷。

translations.literal: His poetry and prose he himself arranged as 《Pine-and-Abacus Hall Collection》; his other writings numbered more than ten kinds as well, nearly a thousand volumes in all.
translations.idiomatic: He selected his own poetry and prose for the 《Pine-and-Abacus Hall Collection》; his other works came to more than ten titles and nearly a thousand volumes.

sentences.zh: 祝允明，字希哲，長洲人。

translations.literal: Zhu Yunming, styled Xizhe, was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yunming, styled Xizhe, came from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖顯，正統四年進士。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xian became a jinshi in the fourth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xian passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 內侍傳旨試能文者四人，顯與焉，入掖門，知欲令教小內豎也，不試而出。

translations.literal: Eunuchs transmitted an order to test four men skilled in writing; Xian was among them; entering the Rear Gate he realized they wished to have him teach young eunuchs, so he did not take the test and walked out.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs relayed an order to test four men of literary talent, and Xian was one of them. Once inside the Rear Gate he saw they meant to make him tutor young eunuchs, so he refused the test and left.

sentences.zh: 由給事中歷山西參政。

translations.literal: He rose from supervising secretary to administration commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced from supervising secretary to administration commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 並有聲。

translations.literal: Both had reputations.
translations.idiomatic: Both were well regarded.

sentences.zh: 允明以弘治五年舉於鄉，久之不第，授廣東興寧知縣。

translations.literal: Yunming passed the provincial examination in the fifth year of Hongzhi; after long failing to pass the metropolitan examination he was appointed magistrate of Xingning in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Yunming passed the provincial examination in Hongzhi 5 but failed repeatedly at the capital; he was eventually appointed magistrate of Xingning in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 捕戮盜魁三十余，邑以無警。

translations.literal: He captured and executed more than thirty bandit chiefs, and the district was free of alarm.
translations.idiomatic: He captured and executed more than thirty bandit leaders, and the district knew peace.

sentences.zh: 稍遷應天通判，謝病歸。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to assistant prefect of Yingtian and returned home citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to assistant prefect of Yingtian, then retired citing illness.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiajing 5.

sentences.zh: 允明生而枝指，故自號枝山，又號枝指生。

translations.literal: Yunming was born with a supernumerary finger; hence he styled himself Zhishan and also styled himself the Supernumerary-Fingered Man.
translations.idiomatic: Yunming was born with an extra finger, and so styled himself Zhishan and also the Supernumerary-Fingered Man.

sentences.zh: 五歲作徑尺字，九歲能詩，稍長，博覽群集，文章有奇氣，當筵疾書，思若涌泉。

translations.literal: At five he could write characters a foot across; at nine he could compose poetry; as he grew older he read widely among collected works; his writing had extraordinary spirit; at a banquet he could write swiftly, his thoughts gushing like a spring.
translations.idiomatic: At five he could write characters a foot high; at nine he wrote poetry. As he matured he read widely, and his prose had a singular force; at banquets he wrote at speed, ideas pouring forth like a spring.

sentences.zh: 尤工書法，名動海內。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in calligraphy, and his fame shook the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially gifted in calligraphy, and his renown spread throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 好酒色六博，善新聲，求文及書者踵至，多賄妓掩得之。

translations.literal: He loved wine, women, and dice; he was skilled in new songs; those seeking his writing and calligraphy arrived in unbroken succession, and he often took bribes from courtesans who concealed themselves to obtain his work.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine, women, and dice, and excelled at new songs. Seekers of his writing and calligraphy came in endless succession, and he often let courtesans bribe their way in to get his work in secret.

sentences.zh: 惡禮法士，亦不問生產，有所入，輒召客豪飲，費盡乃已，或分與持去，不留一錢。

translations.literal: He despised men of ritual and propriety and also paid no heed to making a living; whenever money came in he would summon guests for lavish drinking, not stopping until it was all spent, or he would divide it and let them take it away, not keeping a single coin.
translations.idiomatic: He scorned men of ritual propriety and cared nothing for livelihood. Whenever money came in he summoned guests for grand drinking until it was gone, or divided it among them and kept not a single coin.

sentences.zh: 晚益困，每出，追呼索逋者相隨於後，允明益自喜。

translations.literal: In later years he grew ever more destitute; whenever he went out, bill collectors calling for debts followed behind him, and Yunming was all the more pleased with himself.
translations.idiomatic: In later years he grew poorer still; whenever he went out, debt collectors shouting for payment trailed behind him, and Yunming seemed all the more pleased.

sentences.zh: 所著有詩文集六十卷，他雜著百余卷。

translations.literal: His writings included a collected poetry and prose in sixty volumes and other miscellaneous works of more than a hundred volumes.
translations.idiomatic: His collected poetry and prose ran to sixty volumes, with more than a hundred additional volumes of miscellaneous works.

sentences.zh: 子續，正德中進士，仕至廣西左布政使。

translations.literal: His son Xu became a jinshi in the Zhengde era and served up to left administration commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu became a jinshi in the Zhengde reign and rose to left administration commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 唐寅，字伯虎，一字子畏。

translations.literal: Tang Yin, styled Bohu, with an alternate style Ziwei.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yin, styled Bohu, also known as Ziwei.

sentences.zh: 性穎利，與里狂生張靈縱酒，不事諸生業。

translations.literal: By nature he was quick and sharp; with the mad student of his district Zhang Ling he drank freely and did not attend to his student duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was quick-witted by nature and drank freely with the wild local student Zhang Ling, neglecting his scholarly duties.

sentences.zh: 祝允明規之，乃閉戶浹歲。

translations.literal: Zhu Yunming admonished him, whereupon he shut his door for a full year.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yunming admonished him, and he shut himself indoors for a full year.

sentences.zh: 舉弘治十一年鄉試第一，座主梁儲奇其文，還朝示學士程敏政，敏政亦奇之。

translations.literal: He ranked first in the provincial examination of the eleventh year of Hongzhi; his examiner Liang Chu marveled at his essays and, upon returning to court, showed them to Academician Cheng Minzheng, who also marveled at them.
translations.idiomatic: He placed first in the Hongzhi 11 provincial examination. Examiner Liang Chu was astonished by his essays and, back at court, showed them to Academician Cheng Minzheng, who was equally impressed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，敏政總裁會試，江陰富人徐經賄其家僮，得試題。

translations.literal: Before long Minzheng presided over the metropolitan examination; Xu Jing, a rich man of Jiangyin, bribed his household servant and obtained the examination topics.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Minzheng presided over the metropolitan examination, and Xu Jing, a wealthy man of Jiangyin, bribed his household servant and obtained the examination topics.

sentences.zh: 事露，言者劾敏政，語連寅，下詔獄，謫為吏。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed, critics impeached Minzheng and the words implicated Yin; he was sent to the imperial prison and demoted to clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When the scandal broke, critics impeached Minzheng and the accusations extended to Yin; he was imprisoned by imperial order and reduced to clerk status.

sentences.zh: 寅恥不就，歸家益放浪。

translations.literal: Yin was ashamed and would not accept it; returning home he became all the more unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was too ashamed to accept the demotion and returned home to live ever more freely.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠厚幣聘之，寅察其有異志，佯狂使酒，露其醜穢。

translations.literal: Prince of Ning Chen Hao employed him with rich gifts; Yin saw that he had disloyal ambitions, feigned madness and drank recklessly, and exposed his own shameful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ning Chen Hao tried to hire him with rich gifts, but Yin saw treasonous ambition in him and feigned madness and drunkenness, displaying his own disgraceful behavior.

sentences.zh: 宸濠不能堪，放還。

translations.literal: Chen Hao could not bear it and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hao could not endure it and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 築室桃花塢，與客日般飲其中，年五十四而卒。

translations.literal: He built a dwelling at Peach Blossom Mound and daily drank with guests there; he died at fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He built a house at Peach Blossom Mound and drank there daily with guests; he died at fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 寅詩文，初尚才情，晚年頹然自放，謂後人知我不在此，論者傷之。

translations.literal: Yin's poetry and prose at first prized talent and feeling; in his later years he declined into self-abandonment, saying that posterity would know him not for this, and commentators lamented it.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's poetry and prose at first prized talent and feeling, but in later years he sank into self-abandonment, saying posterity would not remember him for this work, and critics mourned the waste.

sentences.zh: 吳中自枝山輩以放誕不羈為世所指目，而文才輕艷，傾動流輩，傳說者增益而附麗之，往往出名教外。

translations.literal: In Wu, from Zhishan's generation onward they were marked by the world for wild and unrestrained behavior; yet their literary talent was light and brilliant, swaying their contemporaries; storytellers embellished and appended to their tales, often placing them outside the bounds of propriety.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu, from Zhishan's circle onward, these men were noted for wild and unrestrained lives, yet their literary gifts were bright and seductive and swayed their peers; storytellers embellished their legends until they often seemed to stand outside the bounds of propriety.

sentences.zh: 時常熟有桑悅者，字民懌，尤怪妄，亦以才名吳中。

translations.literal: At the time in Changshu there was Sang Yue, styled Minyi, especially strange and presumptuous, also famed in Wu for his talent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time in Changshu there was Sang Yue, styled Minyi, exceptionally eccentric and arrogant, also celebrated in Wu for his talent.

sentences.zh: 書過目，輒焚棄，曰：「已在吾腹中矣。

translations.literal: After books passed before his eyes he would burn and discard them, saying: "They are already in my belly.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had read a book he burned it, saying, "It is already in my belly.

sentences.zh: 」敢為大言，以孟子自況。

translations.literal: " He dared speak great words and compared himself to Mencius.
translations.idiomatic: " He spoke grandly and compared himself to Mencius.

sentences.zh: 或問翰林文章，曰：「虛無人，舉天下惟悅，其次祝允明，又次羅。

translations.literal: When someone asked about Hanlin essays, he said: "Virtually no one; in all the realm there is only Yue; next Zhu Yunming; then Luo Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When asked about Hanlin writing, he said, "There is virtually no one worth mentioning; in all the realm there is only Yue; next comes Zhu Yunming; after that, Luo Qi.

sentences.zh: 」為諸生，上謁監司，曰「江南才子」。

translations.literal: " As a student, when he went up to visit the surveillance commissioner, he called himself "Jiangnan Talent."
translations.idiomatic: " As a student paying a call on the surveillance commissioner, he styled himself "Jiangnan Talent."

sentences.zh: 監司大駭，延之較書，預刊落以試悅，文義不屬者，索筆補之。

translations.literal: The commissioner was greatly alarmed, invited him to compare writings, deliberately excised passages to test Yue; where the text did not connect, Yue demanded a brush and made supplements.
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner was greatly alarmed and invited him to compare texts, deliberately deleting passages to test Yue; where the meaning broke off, Yue asked for a brush and filled in the gaps.

sentences.zh: 年十九舉成化元年鄉試，試春官，答策語不雅訓，被斥。

translations.literal: At nineteen he passed the provincial examination of the first year of Chenghua; when he tried the metropolitan examination his policy essay language was not in proper style and he was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he passed the Chenghua 1 provincial examination, but at the metropolitan examination his policy essay was judged improper in language and he was rejected.

sentences.zh: 三試得副榜，年二十余耳，年籍誤二為六，遂除泰和訓導。

translations.literal: On three tries he made the supplementary list; he was barely over twenty, but in the age register two was mistaken for six, so he was appointed instructor of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: On three attempts he made the supplementary list; he was barely over twenty, but in the age register "two" was mistaken for "six," and he was appointed instructor at Taihe.

sentences.zh: 學士丘浚重其文，屬學使者善遇之。

translations.literal: Academician Qiu Jun prized his writing and instructed the education intendant to treat him well.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Qiu Jun valued his writing and asked the education intendant to treat him kindly.

sentences.zh: 使者至，問：「悅不迎，豈有恙乎？

translations.literal: When the intendant arrived, he asked: "Yue did not come to welcome me—is he unwell?
translations.idiomatic: When the intendant arrived, he asked, "Yue did not come to welcome me—is he ill?

sentences.zh: 」長吏皆銜之，曰：「無恙，自負才名不肯謁耳。

translations.literal: " The chief officials all harbored resentment and said: "He is not unwell; he relies on his literary fame and refuses to pay a visit, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: " The senior officials, who resented Yue, said, "He is not ill; he simply trusts in his literary fame and refuses to pay calls.

sentences.zh: 」使者遣吏召不至，益兩使促之。

translations.literal: " The intendant sent an official to summon him but he did not come; he sent two more envoys to urge him.
translations.idiomatic: " The intendant sent an official to summon him, but Yue did not come; he sent two more messengers to press him.

sentences.zh: 悅怒曰：「始吾謂天下未有無耳者，乃今有之。

translations.literal: Yue angrily said: "At first I thought there was no one under Heaven without ears, but now there is.
translations.idiomatic: Yue angrily said, "I once thought there was no one under Heaven without ears, but now I see there is.

sentences.zh: 與若期，三日後來，瀆則不來矣。

translations.literal: I will make an appointment with you; come three days later—if you offend again I will not come.
translations.idiomatic: I will give you an appointment: come three days from now. If you offend me again, I will not come.

sentences.zh: 」使者恚，欲收悅，緣浚故，不果。

translations.literal: " The intendant was enraged and wished to arrest Yue, but because of Qiu Jun he did not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: " The intendant was furious and wanted to arrest Yue, but because of Qiu Jun he did not.

sentences.zh: 三日來見，長揖使者。

translations.literal: Three days later he came to see him and gave the intendant a long bow.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later he came and gave the intendant a long bow.

sentences.zh: 使者怒，悅脫帽竟去。

translations.literal: The intendant was angry; Yue took off his cap and simply left.
translations.idiomatic: The intendant grew angry; Yue removed his cap and walked off.

sentences.zh: 使者下階謝，乃已。

translations.literal: The intendant went down the steps to apologize, and then it ended.
translations.idiomatic: The intendant came down the steps to apologize, and the matter ended.

sentences.zh: 遷長沙通判，調柳州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to assistant prefect of Changsha and then to Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to assistant prefect of Changsha, then to Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 會外艱歸，遂不出。

translations.literal: When his father died he returned home and then did not go out again.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he returned home and never took office again.

sentences.zh: 居家益狂誕，鄉人莫不重其文，而駭其行。

translations.literal: At home he grew ever more wild and eccentric; the villagers all valued his writing but were shocked by his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: At home he grew ever wilder; his neighbors all respected his writing but were appalled by his behavior.

sentences.zh: 初，悅在京師，見高麗使臣市本朝《兩都賦》，無有，以為恥，遂賦之。

translations.literal: At first, when Yue was in the capital he saw a Goryeo envoy buying the court's 《Rhapsody on the Two Capitals》 and there was none; he took this as a shame and composed one himself.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, while Yue was in the capital, he saw a Goryeo envoy trying to buy the court's 《Rhapsody on the Two Capitals》 and finding none; ashamed, he wrote one himself.

sentences.zh: 居長沙，著《庸言》，自以為窮究天人之際。

translations.literal: While living in Changsha he wrote 《Ordinary Words》 and considered that he had exhaustively investigated the juncture of Heaven and man.
translations.idiomatic: While living in Changsha he wrote 《Ordinary Words》 and believed he had plumbed the meeting point of Heaven and man.

sentences.zh: 所著書，頗行於世。

translations.literal: His writings circulated widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His books circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 邊貢，字廷實，歷城人。

translations.literal: Bian Gong, styled Tingshi, was a native of Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Gong, styled Tingshi, came from Licheng.

sentences.zh: 祖寧，應天治中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ning was magistrate of Yingtian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ning served as magistrate of Yingtian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父節，代州知州。

translations.literal: His father Jie was prefect of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jie was prefect of Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 貢年二十舉於鄉，第弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: Gong passed the provincial examination at twenty and ranked as jinshi in the ninth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Gong passed the provincial examination at twenty and became a jinshi in Hongzhi 9.

sentences.zh: 除太常博士，擢兵科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and promoted to supervising secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 孝宗崩，疏劾中官張瑜，太醫劉文泰、高廷和用藥之謬，又劾中官苗逵、保國公硃暉、都御史史琳用兵之失。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong died, he memorialized impeaching the eunuch Zhang Yu, and the imperial physicians Liu Wenta and Gao Tinghe for errors in administering medicine; he also impeached the eunuch Miao Kui, the Defender Duke of the State Zhu Hui, and Censor-in-Chief Shi Lin for errors in military deployment.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong died, he memorialized against the eunuch Zhang Yu and the imperial physicians Liu Wenta and Gao Tinghe for medical errors, and also against the eunuch Miao Kui, Defender Duke of the State Zhu Hui, and Censor-in-Chief Shi Lin for military failures.

sentences.zh: 改太常丞，遷衛輝知府，改荊州，並能其官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then promoted to prefect of Weihui, then transferred to Jingzhou—all posts at which he proved capable.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then prefect of Weihui, then of Jingzhou, and proved capable in each post.

sentences.zh: 歷陝西、河南提學副使，以母憂家居。

translations.literal: He served as vice education commissioner of Shaanxi and Henan, then stayed at home due to mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice education commissioner in Shaanxi and Henan, then retired home to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖改元，用薦，起南京太常少卿，三遷太常卿，督四夷館，擢刑部右侍郎，拜戶部尚書，並在南京。

translations.literal: When Jiajing changed the reign title, on recommendation he was raised to Vice Director of the Nanjing Court of Imperial Sacrifices, thrice promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, supervised the Four Barbarians Hall, promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments, and appointed Minister of Revenue—all in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing reign began, he was recommended and recalled as Vice Director of the Nanjing Court of Imperial Sacrifices; after three promotions he became its Director, supervised the Four Barbarians Hall, rose to Vice Minister of Punishments, and was appointed Minister of Revenue—all in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 貢早負才名，美風姿，所交悉海內名士。

translations.literal: Gong early bore a reputation for talent and had a handsome bearing; those he befriended were all celebrated men of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Gong won early fame for talent and had a handsome bearing; his friends were celebrated men from across the realm.

sentences.zh: 久官留都，優閒無事，遊覽江山，揮毫浮白，夜以繼日。

translations.literal: Long serving in the secondary capital, he was leisurely with little to do, touring rivers and mountains, wielding the brush and raising cups of wine, continuing day and night.
translations.idiomatic: After long service in the secondary capital he lived at leisure, touring rivers and mountains, writing and drinking, day and night without pause.

sentences.zh: 都御史劾其縱酒廢職，遂罷歸。

translations.literal: The censor-in-chief impeached him for indulging in wine and neglecting duty, and he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The censor-in-chief impeached him for drunken neglect of duty, and he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 顧璘弟 瑮 附 陳沂 等

translations.literal: Gu Lin, younger brother: Bao, with appended biographies: Chen Yi and others.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Lin, with his younger brother Bao and appended biographies of Chen Yi and others.

sentences.zh: 顧璘，字華玉，上元人。

translations.literal: Gu Lin, styled Huayu, was a native of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Lin, styled Huayu, came from Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the ninth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Hongzhi 9.

sentences.zh: 授廣平知縣，擢南京吏部主事，晉郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Guangping, promoted to clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel, and advanced to director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Guangping, then promoted to clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel and advanced to director.

sentences.zh: 正德四年出為開封知府，數與鎮守太監廖堂、王宏忤，逮下錦衣獄，謫全州知州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengde he went out as prefect of Kaifeng; he repeatedly clashed with the garrison eunuchs Liao Tang and Wang Hong, was seized and sent to the Brocade-clad Guard prison, and demoted to magistrate of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 4 he became prefect of Kaifeng; he repeatedly clashed with the garrison eunuchs Liao Tang and Wang Hong, was thrown into the Brocade-clad Guard prison, and demoted to magistrate of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，遷台州知府。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was transferred to prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was transferred to prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 歷浙江左布政使，山西、湖廣巡撫，右副都御史，所至有聲。

translations.literal: He served as left administration commissioner of Zhejiang, grand coordinator of Shanxi and Huguang, and vice censor-in-chief; wherever he went he had a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He served as left administration commissioner of Zhejiang, grand coordinator of Shanxi and Huguang, and vice censor-in-chief, winning renown wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部右侍郎，改工部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel and then changed to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel, then moved to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 董顯陵工畢，遷南京刑部尚書。

translations.literal: When supervision of the Xianling tomb was completed, he was transferred to Minister of Punishments in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: After overseeing completion of the Xianling tomb, he was transferred to Minister of Punishments in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 罷歸，年七十余卒。

translations.literal: He was dismissed and returned home; he died in his seventies.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed and sent home, he died in his seventies.

sentences.zh: 璘少負才名，與何、李相上下。

translations.literal: Lin early bore a reputation for talent and was on a par with He and Li.
translations.idiomatic: Lin won early fame for talent and ranked with He and Li.

sentences.zh: 虛己好士，如恐不及。

translations.literal: He emptied himself to honor scholars, as though fearing he could not reach them soon enough.
translations.idiomatic: He humbled himself before men of talent, as though afraid he might never reach them in time.

sentences.zh: 在浙，慕孫太初一元不可得見。

translations.literal: While in Zhejiang he admired Sun Yiyuan, styled Taichu, and could not obtain a meeting.
translations.idiomatic: While in Zhejiang he admired Sun Yiyuan, styled Taichu, but could never manage to meet him.

sentences.zh: 道衣幅巾，放舟湖上，月下見小舟泊斷橋，一僧、一鶴、一童子煮茗，笑曰：「此必太初也。

translations.literal: Wearing Taoist robes and a headcloth, he put out a boat on the lake; under the moon he saw a small boat moored at Broken Bridge—a monk, a crane, and a boy brewing tea—and laughed, saying: "This must be Taichu.
translations.idiomatic: Dressed in Taoist robes and a scholar's headcloth, he put out on the lake; by moonlight he saw a small boat moored at Broken Bridge—a monk, a crane, and a boy brewing tea—and laughed, "This must be Taichu.

sentences.zh: 」移舟就之，遂往還無間。

translations.literal: " He moved his boat toward them and from then on they visited back and forth without interruption.
translations.idiomatic: " He steered his boat over, and from then on they visited one another constantly.

sentences.zh: 撫湖廣時，愛王廷陳才，欲見之，廷陳不可。

translations.literal: While serving as grand coordinator of Huguang he admired Wang Tingchen's talent and wished to meet him; Tingchen would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: While grand coordinator of Huguang he admired Wang Tingchen's talent and wished to meet him, but Tingchen refused.

sentences.zh: 偵廷陳狎游，疾掩之，廷陳避不得，遂定交。

translations.literal: He spied on Tingchen's casual outings and rushed in to seize him; Tingchen could not escape, and they then formed a friendship.
translations.idiomatic: He spied on Tingchen's casual outings and rushed in to corner him; unable to escape, Tingchen became his friend.

sentences.zh: 既歸，構息園，大治幸舍居客，客常滿。

translations.literal: After returning he built the Rest Garden, greatly renovated guest quarters, and lodgers were always full.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home he built the Rest Garden, greatly expanded the guest quarters, and his house was always full of visitors.

sentences.zh: 從弟瑮，字英玉，以河南副使歸，居園側一小樓，教授自給。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Bao, styled Yingyu, having returned as vice commissioner of Henan, lived in a small tower beside the garden and supported himself by teaching.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Bao, styled Yingyu, returned home after serving as vice commissioner of Henan and lived in a small tower beside the Rest Garden, supporting himself as a teacher.

sentences.zh: 璘時時與客豪飲，伎樂雜作。

translations.literal: Lin would often hold lavish drinking parties with guests, with musicians and entertainers performing together.
translations.idiomatic: Lin often held lavish drinking parties with guests, with musicians and entertainers performing together.

sentences.zh: 呼瑮，瑮終不赴，其孤介如此。

translations.literal: When summoned, Bao never came—such was his aloof integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin summoned him, Bao never came—such was his aloof integrity.

sentences.zh: 初，璘與同里陳沂、王韋，號「金陵三俊」。

translations.literal: At first Lin, together with Chen Yi and Wang Wei of the same district, were styled the "Three Talents of Jinling."
translations.idiomatic: At first Lin, together with Chen Yi and Wang Wei of the same district, were styled the "Three Talents of Jinling."

sentences.zh: 其後寶應朱應登繼起，稱四大家。

translations.literal: Later Zhu Yingdeng of Baoying rose in their wake, and they were called the Four Great Masters.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhu Yingdeng of Baoying rose in their wake, and they were called the Four Great Masters.

sentences.zh: 璘詩，矩矱唐人，以風調勝。

translations.literal: Lin's poetry measured itself against Tang poets and excelled in tone and manner.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's poetry took Tang poets as its measure and excelled in tone and manner.

sentences.zh: 韋婉麗多致，頗失纖弱。

translations.literal: Wei's verse was graceful and rich in import, yet tended somewhat toward excessive delicacy.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's verse was graceful and rich in feeling, yet tended toward excessive delicacy.

sentences.zh: 沂與韋同調。

translations.literal: Yi was of the same school as Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yi wrote in the same vein as Wei.

sentences.zh: 應登才思泉涌，落筆千言。

translations.literal: Yingdeng's talent and thought poured forth like a spring; a thousand words flowed from his brush.
translations.idiomatic: Yingdeng's talent and thought poured forth like a spring, and a thousand words flowed from his brush.

sentences.zh: 然璘、應登羽翼李夢陽，而韋、沂則頗持異論。

translations.literal: Yet Lin and Yingdeng supported Li Mengyang, while Wei and Yi held rather differing views.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lin and Yingdeng supported Li Mengyang, while Wei and Yi held rather different views.

sentences.zh: 三人者，仕宦皆不及璘。

translations.literal: Of the three, none matched Lin in official career.
translations.idiomatic: Of the three, none matched Lin in official advancement.

sentences.zh: 陳沂，字魯南。

translations.literal: Chen Yi, styled Lunan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yi, styled Lunan.

sentences.zh: 正德中進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi during the Zhengde era.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi during the Zhengde era.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士歷編修、侍講，出為江西參議，量移山東參政。

translations.literal: From Hanlin bachelor he rose through compiler and lecturer, went out as commissioner of Jiangxi, and was transferred laterally to administration commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: From Hanlin bachelor he rose through compiler and lecturer, went out as commissioner of Jiangxi, and was later transferred to administration commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 以不附張孚敬、桂萼，改行太僕卿致仕。

translations.literal: Because he would not align with Zhang Fuyi and Gui E, he was reassigned as Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Because he would not align with Zhang Fuyi and Gui E, he was reassigned as Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud and retired.

sentences.zh: 王韋，字欽佩。

translations.literal: Wang Wei, styled Qinpei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei, styled Qinpei.

sentences.zh: 父徽，成化時給事中，直諫有聲。

translations.literal: His father Hui was a censor during the Chenghua era, famous for forthright remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui was a censor during the Chenghua era, renowned for forthright remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 韋舉弘治中進士，由庶吉士歷官太僕少卿。

translations.literal: Wei passed the jinshi examination in the Hongzhi era and, from Hanlin bachelor, rose to Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Wei passed the jinshi examination in the Hongzhi era and, from Hanlin bachelor, rose to Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 子逢元，亦能詩。

translations.literal: His son Fengyuan could also write poetry.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fengyuan could also write poetry.

sentences.zh: 朱應登，字升之。

translations.literal: Zhu Yingdeng, styled Shengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yingdeng, styled Shengzhi.

sentences.zh: 弘治中進士，歷雲南提學副使，遷參政。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the Hongzhi era, served as vice education commissioner of Yunnan, and was promoted to administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the Hongzhi era, served as vice education commissioner of Yunnan, and was promoted to administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 恃才傲物，中飛語，罷歸。

translations.literal: Haughty with his talent and disdainful of others, he fell victim to slander and was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Haughty with his talent and disdainful of others, he fell victim to slander and was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 子日籓，嘉靖間進士，終九江知府。

translations.literal: His son Rifan became a jinshi in the Jiajing era and ended as prefect of Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rifan became a jinshi in the Jiajing era and ended as prefect of Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 能文章，世其家。

translations.literal: Skilled in literary composition, he carried on the family tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in literary composition, he carried on the family tradition.

sentences.zh: 南都自洪、永初，風雅未暢。

translations.literal: Since the Hongwu and Yongle eras, literary refinement in the Southern Capital had not flourished.
