translations.idiomatic: Since the Hongwu and Yongle eras, literary refinement in the Southern Capital had not flourished.

sentences.zh: 徐霖、陳鐸、金琮、謝璿輩談藝正德時，稍稍振起。

translations.literal: Xu Lin, Chen Duo, Jin Cong, Xie Xuan and others, in discussing the arts during the Zhengde era, brought about a slight revival.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Lin, Chen Duo, Jin Cong, Xie Xuan, and others discussed the arts during the Zhengde era, the literary scene stirred slightly.

sentences.zh: 自璘王詞壇，士大夫希風附塵，厥道大彰。

translations.literal: From the time Lin held sway over the literary circle, scholar-officials sought his wind and attached themselves to his dust, and that path was greatly manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lin held sway over the literary circle, scholar-officials sought his example and attached themselves to him, and that path was greatly manifest.

sentences.zh: 許谷，陳鳳，璿子少南，金大車、大輿、金鑾，盛時泰，陳芹之屬，並從之游。

translations.literal: Xu Gu, Chen Feng, Xuan's son Shaonan, Jin Dache, Dayu, and Jin Luan, Sheng Shitai, Chen Qin and the like all associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gu, Chen Feng, Xuan's son Shaonan, Jin Dache, Dayu, and Jin Luan, Sheng Shitai, Chen Qin, and others all associated with him.

sentences.zh: 谷等皆裡人，鑾僑居客也。

translations.literal: Gu and the others were all locals; Luan alone was a sojourning guest.
translations.idiomatic: Gu and the others were all locals; Luan alone was a sojourning guest.

sentences.zh: 儀真蔣山卿、江都趙鶴亦與璘遙相應和。

translations.literal: Jiang Shanqing of Yizhen and Zhao He of Jiangdu also exchanged verses with Lin from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shanqing of Yizhen and Zhao He of Jiangdu also exchanged verses with Lin from afar.

sentences.zh: 沿及末造，風流未歇雲。

translations.literal: Even into the dynasty's final years, the literary current did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Even into the dynasty's final years, the literary current did not cease.

sentences.zh: 鄭善夫附 殷雲霄 方豪 等

translations.literal: Zheng Shanfu, with appended biographies: Yin Yunxiao, Fang Hao, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shanfu, with appended biographies of Yin Yunxiao, Fang Hao, and others.

sentences.zh: 鄭善夫，字繼之，閩縣人。

translations.literal: Zheng Shanfu, styled Jizhi, was a native of Min County.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shanfu, styled Jizhi, came from Min County.

sentences.zh: 弘治十八年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the eighteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Hongzhi 18.

sentences.zh: 連遭內外艱，正德六年始為戶部主事，榷稅滸墅，以清操聞。

translations.literal: After successive bereavements for parents and wife, he became a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue only in the sixth year of Zhengde, collecting taxes at Xushu, and was known for his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: After successive bereavements for parents and wife, he became a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue only in Zhengde 6, collecting taxes at Xushu, and was known for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 時劉瑾雖誅，嬖幸用事。

translations.literal: Though Liu Jin had been executed, favored minions still held power.
translations.idiomatic: Though Liu Jin had been executed, favored minions still held power.

sentences.zh: 善夫憤之，乃告歸，築草堂金鰲峰下，為遲清亭，讀書其中，曰：「俟天下之清也。

translations.literal: Shanfu was indignant, resigned, built a thatched hall beneath Golden Turtle Peak, and made the Awaiting Clarity Pavilion, reading there, and said: "I await the world's clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Indignant, Shanfu resigned, built a thatched hall beneath Golden Turtle Peak, and made the Awaiting Clarity Pavilion, reading there and saying, "I await the world's clarity.

sentences.zh: 」寡交游，日晏未炊，欣然自得。

translations.literal: " He kept few social contacts; even when evening came with no meal cooked, he was content and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: " He kept few social contacts; even when evening came with no meal cooked, he was content and at ease.

sentences.zh: 起禮部主事，進員外郎。

translations.literal: He was recalled as clerk in the Ministry of Rites and advanced to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as clerk in the Ministry of Rites and advanced to vice director.

sentences.zh: 武宗將南巡，偕同列切諫，杖於廷，罰跪五日。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong was about to tour the south, he remonstrated sharply together with colleagues, was beaten at court, and punished to kneel for five days.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong was about to tour the south, he remonstrated sharply together with colleagues, was beaten at court, and punished to kneel for five days.

sentences.zh: 善夫更為疏草，置懷中，屬其僕曰：「死即上之。

translations.literal: Shanfu drafted another memorial, placed it in his bosom, and instructed his servant, saying: "If I die, submit it at once.
translations.idiomatic: Shanfu drafted another memorial, placed it in his bosom, and instructed his servant, saying, "If I die, submit it at once.

sentences.zh: 」幸不死，嘆曰：「時事若此，尚可靦顏就列哉！

translations.literal: " Fortunately he did not die, and sighed, saying: "When affairs are like this, how can one still bear to hold office with a straight face!
translations.idiomatic: " Fortunately he did not die, and sighed, "When affairs are like this, how can one still bear to hold office with a straight face!

sentences.zh: 」乞歸未得，明年力請，乃得歸。

translations.literal: " He requested retirement but was not granted it; the next year he pressed hard, and only then was allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: " He requested retirement but was not granted it; the next year he pressed hard, and only then was allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖改元，用薦起南京刑部郎中，未上，改吏部。

translations.literal: When the Jiajing reign began, he was recalled on recommendation as director in the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments; before taking up the post he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing reign began, he was recalled on recommendation as director in the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments; before taking up the post he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 行抵建寧，便道游武夷、九曲，風雪絕糧，得病卒，年三十有九。

translations.literal: Traveling as far as Jianning, he took a side trip to Mount Wuyi and the Nine Turns; wind and snow cut off his provisions, he fell ill and died, aged thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling as far as Jianning, he took a side trip to Mount Wuyi and the Nine Turns; wind and snow cut off his provisions, he fell ill and died at thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 善夫敦行誼，婚嫁七弟妹，貲悉推予之，葬母黨二十二人。

translations.literal: Shanfu was sincere in friendship and conduct: he arranged marriages for seven younger brothers and sisters and gave them all his assets, and buried twenty-two maternal clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: Shanfu was sincere in friendship and conduct: he arranged marriages for seven younger brothers and sisters and gave them all his assets, and buried twenty-two maternal clansmen.

sentences.zh: 所交盡名士，與孫一元、殷雲霄、方豪尤友善。

translations.literal: Those he befriended were all celebrated men; he was especially close to Sun Yiyuan, Yin Yunxiao, and Fang Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Those he befriended were all celebrated men; he was especially close to Sun Yiyuan, Yin Yunxiao, and Fang Hao.

sentences.zh: 作詩，力摹少陵。

translations.literal: In poetry he strove to model Du Fu of Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In poetry he strove to model Du Fu of Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 雲霄，字近夫，壽張人，善夫同年進士。

translations.literal: Yunxiao, styled Jinfu, was a native of Shouzhang and a jinshi of the same year as Shanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Yunxiao, styled Jinfu, came from Shouzhang and was a jinshi of the same year as Shanfu.

sentences.zh: 作蓄艾堂，聚書數千卷，以作者自命。

translations.literal: He built the Gather Mugwort Hall, collected several thousand volumes of books, and styled himself a creative writer.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Gather Mugwort Hall, collected several thousand volumes of books, and styled himself a creative writer.

sentences.zh: 正德中，官南京給事中。

translations.literal: During the Zhengde era he served as censor in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde era he served as censor in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 武宗納有娠女子馬姬宮中，雲霄偕同官疏諫，引李園、呂不韋事為諷，不報。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong took into the palace Lady Ma, a pregnant woman, Yunxiao joined fellow officials in a memorial remonstrating, citing the cases of Li Yuan and Lü Buwei as admonitory parallels, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong took into the palace Lady Ma, a pregnant woman, Yunxiao joined fellow officials in a memorial remonstrating, citing the cases of Li Yuan and Lü Buwei as admonitory parallels, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 卒官，年三十有七。

translations.literal: He died in office, aged thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 鄉人穆孔暉畏雲霄峭直，曰：「殷子恥不善，不啻負穢然。」

translations.literal: Fellow townsman Mu Konghui, who feared Yunxiao's stern uprightness, said: "Yinzi is ashamed of what is not good—nothing less than as though carrying filth on his back."
translations.idiomatic: Fellow townsman Mu Konghui, who feared Yunxiao's stern uprightness, said, "Yinzi is ashamed of what is not good—nothing less than as though carrying filth on his back."

sentences.zh: 方豪，字思道，開化人。

translations.literal: Fang Hao, styled Sidao, was a native of Kaihua.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Hao, styled Sidao, came from Kaihua.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Zhengde 3.

sentences.zh: 除崑山知縣，遷刑部主事。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Kunshan, he was transferred to clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed magistrate of Kunshan, he was transferred to clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 諫武宗南巡，跪闕下五日，復受杖。

translations.literal: He remonstrated against Emperor Wuzong's southern tour, kneeling beneath the palace gate for five days, and was beaten again.
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated against Emperor Wuzong's southern tour, kneeling beneath the palace gate for five days, and was beaten again.

sentences.zh: 歷官湖廣副使，罷歸。

translations.literal: He served as vice commissioner of Huguang and was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice commissioner of Huguang and was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 一元，見《隱逸傳》。

translations.literal: Yiyuan is treated in the 《Records of Recluses》.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyuan is treated in the 《Records of Recluses》.

sentences.zh: 閩中詩文，自林鴻、高棅後，閱百餘年，善夫繼之。

translations.literal: Fujian poetry and prose, after Lin Hong and Gao Bing, passed more than a hundred years before Shanfu succeeded them.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian poetry and prose, after Lin Hong and Gao Bing, languished for more than a hundred years before Shanfu revived the tradition.

sentences.zh: 迨萬曆中年，曹學佺、徐勃輩繼起，謝肇淛、鄧原岳和之，風雅復振焉。

translations.literal: By the middle of the Wanli era, Cao Xuequan, Xu Bi Bo, and others rose in turn; Xie Zhaozhe and Deng Yuanyue harmonized with them, and literary refinement was revived.
translations.idiomatic: By the middle of the Wanli era, Cao Xuequan, Xu Bi Bo, and others rose in turn; Xie Zhaozhe and Deng Yuanyue harmonized with them, and literary refinement was revived.

sentences.zh: 學佺詳見後傳。

translations.literal: Xuequan is treated in detail in a later biography.
translations.idiomatic: Xuequan is treated in detail in a later biography.

sentences.zh: 勃，字興公，閩縣人。

translations.literal: Bi Bo, styled Xinggong, was a native of Min County.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Bo, styled Xinggong, came from Min County.

sentences.zh: 兄熥，萬曆間舉人。

translations.literal: His elder brother Cong became a provincial graduate during the Wanli era.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Cong became a provincial graduate during the Wanli era.

sentences.zh: 勃以布衣終。

translations.literal: Bi Bo ended his days as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Bo ended his days as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 博聞多識，善草隸書。

translations.literal: Broadly learned and well informed, he was skilled in cursive and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned and well informed, he was skilled in cursive and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 積書鰲峰書舍至數萬卷。

translations.literal: He accumulated books in the Golden Turtle Peak Bookroom to tens of thousands of volumes.
translations.idiomatic: He accumulated tens of thousands of volumes in the Golden Turtle Peak Bookroom.

sentences.zh: 肇淛，字在杭。

translations.literal: Zhaozhe, styled Zaihang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozhe, styled Zaihang.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三十年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the thirtieth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Wanli 30.

sentences.zh: 官工部郎中，視河張秋，作《北河紀略》，具載河流原委及歷代治河利病。

translations.literal: He served as director in the Ministry of Works, inspected the river at Zhangqiu, and wrote the 《Northern River Gazetteer》, fully recording the river's origins and the benefits and harms of river control through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director in the Ministry of Works, inspected the river at Zhangqiu, and wrote the 《Northern River Gazetteer》, fully recording the river's origins and the benefits and harms of river control through the ages.

sentences.zh: 終廣西右布政使。

translations.literal: He ended as Right Administration Commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as Right Administration Commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 原岳，字汝高，亦閩縣人，肇淛同年進士，終湖廣副使。

translations.literal: Yuanyue, styled Rugao, was also a native of Min County and a jinshi of the same year as Zhaozhe; he ended as vice commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyue, styled Rugao, also came from Min County and was a jinshi of the same year as Zhaozhe; he ended as vice commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 陸深附:王圻

translations.literal: Lu Shen, with appended biography: Wang Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shen, with appended biography of Wang Qi.

sentences.zh: 陸深，字子淵，上海人。

translations.literal: Lu Shen, styled Ziyuan, was a native of Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shen, styled Ziyuan, came from Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 弘治十八年進士，二甲第一。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the eighteenth year of Hongzhi, ranking first in the second class.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Hongzhi 18, ranking first in the second class.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: Selected as Hanlin bachelor, he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as Hanlin bachelor, he was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾嫉翰林官亢己，悉改外，深得南京主事。

translations.literal: Liu Jin resented that Hanlin officials put themselves above him and changed them all to outside posts; Shen was assigned chief clerk in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin resented that Hanlin officials put themselves above him and reassigned them all to outside posts; Shen was assigned chief clerk in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，復職，歷國子司業、祭酒，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, Shen was restored to office, served as vice director and chancellor of the Imperial Academy, and served as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was executed, Shen was restored to office, served as vice director and chancellor of the Imperial Academy, and served as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 奏講官撰進講章，閣臣不宜改竄。

translations.literal: He memorialized that lecturers should draft and submit lecture chapters, and that grand secretaries should not alter them.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that lecturers should draft and submit lecture chapters, and that grand secretaries should not alter them.

sentences.zh: 忤輔臣，謫延平同知。

translations.literal: Offending the chief minister, he was demoted to vice prefect of Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: Offending the chief minister, he was demoted to vice prefect of Yanping.

sentences.zh: 晉山西提學副使，改浙江。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice education commissioner of Shanxi and then transferred to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice education commissioner of Shanxi and then transferred to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 累官四川左布政使。

translations.literal: He rose through successive posts to Left Administration Commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Left Administration Commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 松、茂諸番亂，深主調兵食，有功，賜金幣。

translations.literal: When the tribes of Song and Mao rebelled, Shen advocated mobilizing troops and provisions, had merit, and was rewarded with gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribes of Song and Mao rebelled, Shen advocated mobilizing troops and provisions, distinguished himself, and was rewarded with gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十六年召為太常卿兼侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jiajing he was summoned as Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and Reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 16 he was summoned as Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and Reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 世宗南巡，深掌行在翰林院印，御筆刪侍讀二字，進詹事府詹事，致仕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong toured the south, Shen held the seal of the Hanlin Academy at the traveling palace; the emperor in his own hand struck out the two characters "Reader-in-waiting," and Shen was promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent's Household and retired.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong toured the south, Shen held the seal of the Hanlin Academy at the traveling palace; the emperor in his own hand struck out the two characters "Reader-in-waiting," and Shen was promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent's Household and retired.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡文裕。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously titled Wenyu.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously titled Wenyu.

sentences.zh: 深少與徐禎卿相切磨，為文章有名。

translations.literal: In youth Shen closely refined his craft with Xu Zhenqing and won fame for his literary compositions.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Shen closely refined his craft with Xu Zhenqing and won fame for his literary compositions.

sentences.zh: 工書，仿李邕、趙孟頫。

translations.literal: Skilled in calligraphy, he modeled Li Yong and Zhao Mengfu.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in calligraphy, he modeled Li Yong and Zhao Mengfu.

sentences.zh: 嘗鑒博雅，為詞臣冠。

translations.literal: Once assessed for broad learning and refinement, he was foremost among literary officials.
translations.idiomatic: Once assessed for broad learning and refinement, he was foremost among literary officials.

sentences.zh: 然頗倨傲，人以此少之。

translations.literal: Yet he was rather haughty, and for this people thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was rather haughty, and for this people thought less of him.

sentences.zh: 同邑有王圻者，字元翰。

translations.literal: In the same district there was Wang Qi, styled Yuanhan.
translations.idiomatic: In the same district there was Wang Qi, styled Yuanhan.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十四年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the forty-fourth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Jiajing 44.

sentences.zh: 除清江知縣，調萬安。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Qingjiang, he was transferred to Wan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed magistrate of Qingjiang, he was transferred to Wan'an.

sentences.zh: 擢御史，忤時相，出為福建按察僉事，謫邛州判官。

translations.literal: Promoted to censor, he offended the chief minister of the time, went out as surveillance commissioner of Fujian, and was demoted to assistant magistrate of Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to censor, he offended the chief minister of the time, went out as surveillance commissioner of Fujian, and was demoted to assistant magistrate of Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 兩知進賢、曹縣，遷開州知州。

translations.literal: Twice serving as magistrate of Jinxian and Cao County, he was transferred to prefect of Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Twice serving as magistrate of Jinxian and Cao County, he was transferred to prefect of Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 歷官陝西布政參議，乞養歸，築室淞江之濱，種梅萬樹，目曰梅花源。

translations.literal: He served as administration commissioner of Shaanxi, requested leave to support his parents and returned home, built a house on the banks of the Song River, planted ten thousand plum trees, and named it Plum Blossom Source.
translations.idiomatic: He served as administration commissioner of Shaanxi, requested leave to support his parents and returned home, built a house on the banks of the Song River, planted ten thousand plum trees, and named it Plum Blossom Source.

sentences.zh: 以著書為事，年逾耄耋，猶篝燈帳中，丙夜不輟。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to writing books; past eighty, he still kept a lamp burning in his tent at the third watch of the night without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to writing books; past eighty, he still kept a lamp burning in his tent at the third watch of the night without ceasing.

sentences.zh: 所撰《續文獻通考》諸書行世。

translations.literal: The books he wrote, such as the 《Continuation of the Comprehensive Examination of Literature》, circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: The books he wrote, such as the 《Continuation of the Comprehensive Examination of Literature》, circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 初，圻以奏議為趙貞吉所推。

translations.literal: At first Qi was recommended for his memorials by Zhao Zhenji.
translations.idiomatic: At first Qi was recommended for his memorials by Zhao Zhenji.

sentences.zh: 張居正與貞吉交惡，諷圻攻之，不應。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng was on bad terms with Zhenji and urged Qi to attack him, but Qi would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng feuded with Zhenji and pressed Qi to attack him, but Qi refused.

sentences.zh: 高拱為圻座主，時方修隙徐階，又以圻為私其鄉人不助己，不能無恚，遂摭拾之。

translations.literal: Gao Gong had been Qi's chief examiner; he was then at odds with Xu Jie and, because he thought Qi favored his fellow townsman and would not help him, could not but resent him and seized on pretexts to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gong, who had examined Qi, was then feuding with Xu Jie; he also believed Qi was protecting a fellow townsman and withholding support from him, and in resentment found grounds to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 王廷陳

translations.literal: Wang Tingchen
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingchen

sentences.zh: 王廷陳，字穉欽，黃岡人。

translations.literal: Wang Tingchen, style name Zhiqin, was a native of Huanggang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingchen, whose style name was Zhiqin, came from Huanggang.

sentences.zh: 父濟，吏部郎中。

translations.literal: His father Ji served as director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji was a director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 廷陳穎慧絕人，幼好弄，父抶之，輒大呼曰：「大人奈何虐天下名士！

translations.literal: Tingchen was exceptionally clever beyond others; as a child he loved mischief, and when his father beat him he would shout, "Father, how can you abuse a famous scholar of the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: Tingchen was prodigiously clever; as a boy he loved pranks, and when his father thrashed him he would cry out, "Father, how can you mistreat a famous scholar of the empire!"

sentences.zh: 」正德十二年成進士，選庶吉士，益恃才放恣。

translations.literal: " In the twelfth year of Zhengde he became a presented scholar, was selected as Hanlin bachelor, and grew ever more reckless in relying on his talent.
translations.idiomatic: " He passed the examinations in the twelfth year of Zhengde, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and became still more insolent in his self-confidence.

sentences.zh: 故事，兩學士為館師，體嚴重，廷陳伺其退食，獨上樹杪，大聲叫呼。

translations.literal: By precedent two academicians served as academy instructors with grave dignity; Tingchen waited until they had left for their meal, climbed alone to the treetops, and shouted loudly.
translations.idiomatic: By custom two academicians served as Hanlin instructors with stern dignity; Tingchen waited until they had gone to eat, then climbed a tree alone and yelled at the top of his voice.

sentences.zh: 兩學士無如之何，佯弗聞也。

translations.literal: The two academicians could do nothing about it and pretended not to hear.
translations.idiomatic: The two instructors could do nothing and pretended not to hear.

sentences.zh: 武宗下詔南巡，與同館舒芬等七人將疏諫，館師石珤力止之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong issued an edict for a southern tour, Tingchen and seven others of the same academy, including Shu Fen, were about to submit a memorial of remonstrance, but the academy instructor Shi Yao strongly stopped them.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ordered a southern tour, Tingchen and seven fellow bachelors, including Shu Fen, prepared to remonstrate by memorial, but their instructor Shi Yao forcibly dissuaded them.

sentences.zh: 廷陳賦《烏母謠》，大書於壁以刺，珤及執政皆不悅。

translations.literal: Tingchen composed the 《Ballad of the Crow Mother》, wrote it large on the wall as satire, and Yao and the chief ministers were all displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Tingchen wrote the 《Ballad of the Crow Mother》 in large characters on the wall as a satirical barb, to the displeasure of Yao and the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 已而疏上，帝怒，罰跪五日，杖於廷。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the memorial went up; the emperor was angry, punished them with five days kneeling, and had them beaten at court.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was furious, ordered them to kneel for five days, and had them beaten in court.

sentences.zh: 時已改吏科給事中，乃出為裕州知州。

translations.literal: By then he had been transferred to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, but was sent out as magistrate of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He had already been made supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, but was now sent out as magistrate of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 廷陳不習為吏，又失職怨望，簿牒堆案，漫不省視。

translations.literal: Tingchen was unused to serving as an official and, resentful at losing his post, let documents pile on his desk and paid no attention to them.
translations.idiomatic: Unused to administrative work and bitter over his demotion, he let papers pile up on his desk and ignored them entirely.

sentences.zh: 夏日裸跣坐堂皇，見飛鳥集庭樹，輒止訟者，取彈彈之。

translations.literal: In summer he sat barefoot and bare-chested in the hall of audience; when he saw birds alight in the courtyard trees he would stop litigants, take a pellet bow, and shoot at them.
translations.idiomatic: In summer he sat naked and barefoot in the yamen hall; when birds settled in the courtyard trees he would halt lawsuits, take a pellet bow, and shoot at them.

sentences.zh: 上官行部，不出迎。

translations.literal: When superiors toured the prefecture he did not go out to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: When superiors made inspection tours he refused to go out and receive them.

sentences.zh: 已而布政使陳鳳梧及巡按御史喻茂堅先後至，廷陳以鳳梧座主，特出迓。

translations.literal: Later the administration commissioner Chen Fengwu and the touring censor Yu Maojian arrived in succession; because Fengwu had been Tingchen's chief examiner, he went out especially to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Later the administration commissioner Chen Fengwu and the touring censor Yu Maojian arrived in turn; Tingchen made a special point of going out to greet Fengwu, who had examined him.

sentences.zh: 鳳梧好謂曰：「子候我固善，御史即來，候之當倍謹。

translations.literal: Fengwu kindly said to him, "It is well that you waited on me, but the censor is coming next; you should wait on him with twice the care."
translations.idiomatic: Fengwu said kindly, "It is good that you received me, but the censor is coming next—you should receive him with twice the courtesy."

sentences.zh: 」廷陳許諾。

translations.literal: " Tingchen promised he would.
translations.idiomatic: " Tingchen agreed.

sentences.zh: 及茂堅至，銜其素驕蹇，有意裁抑之，以小過榜州吏。

translations.literal: When Maojian arrived, resenting Tingchen's habitual arrogance, he deliberately sought to humble him and had a minor fault punished by beating a prefectural clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Maojian arrived, bearing a grudge against Tingchen's habitual arrogance, he deliberately sought to put him down and had a clerk beaten for a trifling offense.

sentences.zh: 廷陳為跪請，茂堅故益甚。

translations.literal: Tingchen knelt to plead on the clerk's behalf, and Maojian deliberately made it worse.
translations.idiomatic: Tingchen knelt to intercede, and Maojian deliberately intensified the punishment.

sentences.zh: 廷陳大罵曰：「陳公誤我。

translations.literal: Tingchen cursed loudly, saying, "Master Chen has misled me."
translations.idiomatic: Tingchen burst out cursing, "Master Chen misled me!"

sentences.zh: 」直上堂搏茂堅，悉呼吏卒出，鎖其門，禁絕供億，且將具奏。

translations.literal: " He rushed straight into the hall and struck Maojian, called all clerks and runners out, locked the gates, cut off supplies, and was about to draft a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " He stormed into the hall and attacked Maojian, sent all clerks and runners out, locked the gates, cut off his supplies, and prepared to lodge a memorial against him.

sentences.zh: 茂堅大窘，鳳梧為解，乃夜馳去。

translations.literal: Maojian was greatly embarrassed; Fengwu mediated, and he fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Maojian was utterly humiliated; Fengwu intervened, and he fled overnight.

sentences.zh: 尋上疏劾之，適裕人被案者逸出，奏廷陳不法事，收捕系獄，削籍歸。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he submitted a memorial impeaching Tingchen; just then a prisoner under investigation in Yuzhou escaped and reported Tingchen's illegal conduct; he was arrested, imprisoned, stripped of registry, and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized against Tingchen; meanwhile a prisoner under investigation in Yuzhou escaped and reported Tingchen's misconduct; Tingchen was arrested, imprisoned, struck from the rolls, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 世宗踐阼，前直諫被謫者悉復官，獨廷陳以畦吏議不與。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, all who had been banished for direct remonstrance were restored to office, but Tingchen alone was excluded on the grounds of misconduct as a petty official.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing emperor ascended the throne, all who had been banished for bold remonstrance were restored—except Tingchen, excluded on account of his misconduct as a local magistrate.

sentences.zh: 屏居二十餘年，嗜酒縱倡樂，益自放廢。

translations.literal: Living in seclusion for more than twenty years, he loved wine and indulged in entertainers and music, abandoning himself ever more.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years in retirement he drank heavily, kept singers and musicians, and sank ever deeper into self-abandonment.

sentences.zh: 士大夫造謁，多蓬髮赤足，不具賓主禮。

translations.literal: When scholar-officials came to call, he was often disheveled and barefoot and observed no host-and-guest etiquette.
translations.idiomatic: When gentlemen came to visit, he often received them with tangled hair and bare feet, without proper ceremony.

sentences.zh: 時衣紅紫窄袖衫，騎牛跨馬，嘯歌田野間。

translations.literal: At times he wore narrow-sleeved red and purple shirts, rode oxen or horses, and sang freely in the fields.
translations.idiomatic: He would wear tight-sleeved red and purple shirts, ride oxen or horses, and sing his way through the countryside.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十八年詔修《承天大志》，巡撫顧璘以廷陳及顏木、王格薦。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Jiajing an edict ordered compilation of the 《Great Record of Chengtian》; Grand Coordinator Gu Lin recommended Tingchen together with Yan Mu and Wang Ge.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Jiajing the court ordered compilation of the 《Great Record of Chengtian》; Gu Lin recommended Tingchen along with Yan Mu and Wang Ge.

sentences.zh: 書成，不稱旨，賜銀幣而已。

translations.literal: When the book was completed it did not please the emperor, and they were given only silver and silk coins.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished it failed to please the emperor, and they received only silver and silk in reward.

sentences.zh: 廷陳才高，詩文重當世，一時才士鮮能過之。

translations.literal: Tingchen's talent was high; his poetry and prose were weighty in his age, and few talented men of the time could surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: Tingchen was formidably gifted; his poetry and prose commanded his age, and few contemporaries could match him.

sentences.zh: 木，應山人，官亳州知州。

translations.literal: Mu was from Yingshan and served as magistrate of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mu came from Yingshan and served as magistrate of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 格，京山人，官河南僉事。

translations.literal: Ge was from Jingshan and served as vice commissioner in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Ge came from Jingshan and served as vice commissioner in Henan.

sentences.zh: 李濂，字川父，祥符人。

translations.literal: Li Lian, style name Chuanfu, was a native of Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lian, whose style name was Chuanfu, came from Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 舉正德八年鄉試第一，明年成進士。

translations.literal: He placed first in the provincial examination in the eighth year of Zhengde and became a presented scholar the following year.
translations.idiomatic: He topped the provincial examinations in the eighth year of Zhengde and passed the palace examinations the next year.

sentences.zh: 授沔陽知州，稍遷寧波同知，擢山西僉事。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Mianyang, later transferred to be vice prefect of Ningbo, and promoted to vice commissioner in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Mianyang, later made vice prefect of Ningbo, and then promoted to vice commissioner in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年以大計免歸，年才三十有八。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiajing he was dismissed on the great assessment and returned home at only thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jiajing he was retired on the triennial evaluation and went home at only thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 濂少負俊才，時從俠少年聯騎出城，搏獸射雉，酒酣悲歌，慨然慕信陵君、侯生之為人。

translations.literal: Lian in youth possessed outstanding talent; he often rode out of the city with gallant young men, wrestled beasts and shot pheasants, sang mournfully when wine was warm, and sighed that he admired the conduct of Lord Xinling and Hou Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Lian was brilliantly gifted; he often rode out with swashbuckling companions to wrestle game and shoot pheasants, and when wine had warmed him he would sing sadly, longing to live like Lord Xinling and Hou Sheng.

sentences.zh: 一日作《理情賦》，友人左國璣持以示李夢陽，夢陽大嗟賞，訪之吹台，濂自此聲馳河、雒間。

translations.literal: One day he wrote the 《Rhapsody on Regulating Emotion》; his friend Zuo Guoji showed it to Li Mengyang, who greatly admired it, sought him out at Chuitai, and from then Lian's fame spread between the Yellow and Luo rivers.
translations.idiomatic: One day he wrote the 《Rhapsody on Regulating Emotion》; his friend Zuo Guoji showed it to Li Mengyang, who was deeply impressed, sought him out at Chuitai, and from then Lian's reputation spread throughout the Yellow and Luo region.

sentences.zh: 既罷歸，益肆力於學，遂以古文名於時。

translations.literal: After he was dismissed and returned home he devoted himself still more to study and soon became famed in his time for ancient-style prose.
translations.idiomatic: After his retirement he threw himself into study and soon won fame for his classical prose.

sentences.zh: 初受知夢陽，後不屑附和。

translations.literal: At first he won Mengyang's recognition, but later disdained to follow along with him.
translations.idiomatic: He first won Mengyang's patronage, but later refused to follow his school.

sentences.zh: 里居四十餘年，著述甚富。

translations.literal: Living at home for more than forty years, he wrote abundantly.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for more than forty years and left a very large body of writings.
